1.name: Bijan Robinson
1.comment: Robinson had his second straight huge season. He was second overall in fantasy running back scoring. Robinson had double-digit fantasy points all but a game. He had nine games with 20-plus points. Robinson had a league high 2,298 total yards. He also scored 11 touchdowns. The big difference for Robinson was a bigger role in the passing game, having 79 receptions for 820 yards. He got more work as a pass catcher. Robinson even lost out on some goal-line work to Tyler Allgeier, so his fantasy numbers could have been even better. Robinson has 1,850-plus total yards two straight seasons. He might be the best overall back in the game right now now and is in the prime of his career. Robinson will continue to be the focal point of the Falcons offense. Robinson is the complete package. He is a three-down back that does well on the inside and outside. He also catches the ball very well. Robinson is a big-play back that has great moves in the open field. He does try to make the big play a little too much, missing out on some yards, but improved in that area. And he makes plays after contact, averaging 2.2 yards per carry after contact for his career.
1.outlook: Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson turned in a stellar 2025 campaign, totaling nearly 2,300 yards from scrimmage and 11 touchdowns. While it may be difficult to envision a significant leap from those numbers, there are still reasons to believe the 24-year-old's best football is ahead of him. Former backfield mate Tyler Allgeier, now a member of the Arizona Cardinals, logged at least 135 carries in each of the past three seasons and scored eight rushing touchdowns in 2025 compared to Robinson's seven. Atlanta did add veteran running back Brian Robinson Jr. this offseason, but his one-year, $2.5 million contract indicates that he will, at most, occupy the change-of-pace role vacated by Allgeier. Additionally, the Falcons will be led by two-time AP NFL Coach of the Year Kevin Stefanski in 2026. During Stefanski's tenure in Cleveland, Nick Chubb finished as a top-12 fantasy option three times despite offering limited value as a pass-catcher. Robinson's versatile three-down skill set should allow Stefanski to maximize his usage, especially considering the coach's willingness to involve running backs in the passing game. There's a strong argument for Robinson to be selected first overall in drafts across all formats, so fantasy gamers should be ecstatic whenever they have the opportunity to draft him.

2.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
2.comment: Gibbs had his second straight huge fantasy season, finishing third overall in fantasy running back scoring. He was a little more up and down, though, having fewer than double-digit fantasy points four times. But he did have seven games with 20-plus points, having plenty of big games along the way. Gibbs had 1,839 total yards and 18 touchdowns. He averaged 5.0 yards per carry, making that all three years in the NFL having at least a 5.0 yards per carry averaging. If there was a knock on Gibbs, he did not make a lot of plays after contact, averaging just 1.7 yards per carry after contact. Gibbs will continue to be a huge part of the Lions offense and could play even more of a featured role this year with David Montgomery gone. Gibbs might be the best big-play back in football. He can be a huge asset in the running and passing game. He is a true three-down back. He isn't a huge back but runs with power ands game-breaking speed. Gibbs is one of the top pass-catching backs in the game in addition to being a great runner.
2.outlook: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has finished as the RB4 and RB2 over the past two seasons, and with David Montgomery being traded to the Texans at the beginning of the 2026 offseason, RotoBaller is expecting enough of a workload increase to make Gibbs the number one overall player in non-superflex redraft leagues. In their three seasons together, Montgomery saw over 14 opportunities per game and a total of 48 carries from within the five-yard line. By contrast, free-agent acquisition Isiah Pacheco frequently took a back seat to a past-his-prime Kareem Hunt in their 18 games together, and he did not earn a single goal-line carry in his final season with the Chiefs. 2026 marks year six of the Dan Campbell regime, with the team turning in a top-five offensive finish in each of the past four seasons. Even in what was considered a down year for the unit as it adjusted to life without offensive coordinator Ben Johnson in 2025, the Lions averaged more than 370 yards per game while scoring 56 touchdowns, with Gibbs alone responsible for almost 30% of that yardage total and 18 touchdowns. Detroit's schedule sees the team lined up against some of the worst run defenses in the league by 2025 EPA metrics, and with Gibbs expected to see the heaviest volume of his young career, he could become only the third player in the last decade to top 2,000 scrimmage yards and 20 touchdowns.

3.name: Christian McCaffrey
3.comment: McCaffrey was back to his old ways last year, posting a huge season. He led all of fantasy running backs in scoring, finishing nearly 50 points ahead of the second place finisher. McCaffrey had 22-plus fantasy points seven straight games to start his season. He had 20-plus points 11 of 17 games. McCaffrey had 2,126 total yards, 17 total touchdowns and 102 receptions. He topped 100 receptions for the first time since 2019. McCaffrey did have a career high 413 touches during the regular season. He also had 37 touches in the playoffs, putting him at 450 for the entire season. This is a bit of a concern for him going forward. He is 30 years old and has a history of injury. Another slight red flag is McCaffrey broke just 10 tackles on all those touches and a averaged 1.5 yards after contact. The yards after contact average was the worst of his career. This could show some signs of slowing down a little. He will remain the starting back for the explosive 49ers offense and should get plenty of touches in that role. McCaffrey has double-digit touchdowns three of four seasons and 2,000-plus total yards three of six. McCaffrey has great moves in space and is a very tough tackle in the open field. McCaffrey has great hands and runs top routes for a running back, playing more like a seasoned receiver when getting a chance to catch the ball. He is one of the best all-around backs in the game.
3.outlook: For any rookie looking to make an immediate impact, it comes down to opportunity. For homegrown Eli Heidenreich, the jack-of-all-trades has an interesting path to fantasy relevance in Pittsburgh. During his three-year career at Navy, Heidenreich amassed 1,157 rushing yards, averaging 6.8 yards per carry while being a focal point in the passing game, where he finished with 109 receptions for 1,994 yards, averaging an impressive 18.3 yards per reception. As we head into the 2026 season, Heidenreich has already been spotted working out of the Steelers' backfield as well as lining up both outside and in the slot. Heidenreich's combination of speed (4.44 40-time) and agility, along with his ability to catch the ball, has drawn some comparison to Christian McCaffrey. At Heidenreich's Pro Day, the former service academy product ran a 6.55 three-cone. Over the last 25 years, only three backs have bested that mark at the combine: Chris Rainey, Ray Rice, and McCaffrey. Scouts aren't saying he is McCaffrey, but rather that he has the tools and skillset to offer the Steelers some of the things that McCaffrey has made a living doing. Heidenreich is too valuable not to see action, and with Aaron Rodgers getting up there in age, Heidenreich offers a big-play threat on every dump pass.

4.name: Ashton Jeanty
4.comment: Jeanty probably didn't have quite the rookie year most hoped but it wasn't terrible. He was 11th overall in fantasy running back scoring. Jeanty had 10 of 17 games with double-digit fantasy points, including two games with 30-plus points. He showed his big-game potential as a rookie. Jeanty failed to reach the 1,000-yard rushing mark and averaged just 3.7 yards per carry. He had 1,321 total yards and 10 touchdowns. Jeanty averaged just 1.6 yards before contact, which was the fifth worst total in football. This shows the Raiders offensive line did a really poor job blocking for Jeanty. Hopefully, a new coaching staff and some help along the offensive line will lead to better numbers for Jeanty in year two. He is going to get a big workload in this offense. New head coach Klint Kubiak has a ton of success running the ball, which is great news for Jeanty. Jeanty isn't a huge back but breaks tackles and is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands. He hits the hole in a hurry and has good moves in the open field. Jeanty also catches the ball very well and can be a top three-down back. He does lack some elite speed but that shouldn't hold him back much in the NFL.
4.outlook: Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty produced mixed results week over week in 2025, but he ultimately finished his rookie campaign as the overall RB11 in PPR leagues with 975 rushing yards, 55 catches, 346 receiving yards, and 10 touchdowns. That was on par with his draft capital in redraft leagues, and we'd expect him to make a significant jump in 2026, especially after the Raiders' offseason focused on improving the offense. Most notably, the Raiders brought in quarterbacks Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza. At the very least, Cousin offers a veteran presence to limit turnovers, deliver passes, and hand the ball off a ton. That bodes well for Jeanty, who is running behind an improved offensive line that now features Tyler Linderbaum and Spencer Burford. Meanwhile, Jeanty should also benefit from playing with Mendoza once he ends up taking over for Cousins. Mendoza is a high-upside quarterback with impressive passing skills and the ability to run a dynamic offense. Jeanty stands to benefit both as a ball-carrier and a receiver, giving him upside in all fantasy formats. As long as he stays healthy in Year 2, we would expect Jeanty to finish even higher than last year's rank as RB11. At the moment, he has an ADP of 11.2, which makes him the fifth running back off the board in redraft leagues.

5.name: Devon Achane
5.comment: Achane was a bright spot on a Dolphins team that struggled at times offensively. He had a big season, finishing fifth overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had double-digit fantasy points every single game. His lowest point total of the season was 12.8 points. Achane showed great consistency all season long. Achane had a career-high 1,838 total yards and 12 touchdowns. He had his first 1,000-yard rushing season as a pro. Achane led the league in yards per carry (5.7) and yards after contact, averaging 3.0 yards per carry after contact. He showed he is more than just a finesse back. Achane has double-digit touchdowns all three seasons in the NFL and 1,450-plus total yards two straight. He will continue to be the lead back for the Dolphins and get plenty of touches in that role. Achane is a small back, but has a great speed and big-play ability. He can get to the next level in a hurry and has great moves in space. He runs well between the tackles despite lacking a little size for the position. He will drop some passes and his small size is a bit of a concern for his durability, but he has been able to handle a full workload the last two seasons.
5.outlook: Achane is a top-10 fantasy back, showing great consistency because of his dual-threat ability. Achane is capable of finishing first overall in fantasy running back scoring if all goes right for him. He can get around 1,800 total yards, 70 catches and double-digit scores.

6.name: Jonathan Taylor
6.comment: Taylor had a great season, rebounding some from a somewhat disappointing season. He was fourth overall in fantasy running back scoring. Taylor led the league in rushing touchdowns (18) and ran for 1,585 yards. He was 37 yards shy of his second 2,000 total yard season. Taylor had double-digit fantasy points all but two games and 20-plus points seven times. Taylor has two straight seasons with 1,500-plus total yards. He has 1,000-yard rushing seasons four of six. Taylor remains an elite back and will be a big part of the Colts offense. He is a complete back that can play three downs. He is a top athlete that can carry the load. He catches the ball well and can make plays between the tackles. Taylor also has very good speed and the ability to make plenty of plays on the outside.
6.outlook: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor was one of the top running backs in fantasy football most of last season after rushing for 1,356 yards on 247 attempts with 16 touchdowns across 13 games. He added 35 catches for 304 receiving yards and two scores. The 27-year-old was on the verge of a career-year until quarterback Daniel Jones (Achilles) suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in Week 14 against the Jaguars. Once Jones went down, Taylor ended with just 229 rushing yards and two scores while averaging just 3.0 yards per carry in his last four games. His fantasy value relies a lot on whether or not Jones is fully healthy. Jones is progressing well in his recovery from a torn Achilles and is expected to be ready for Week 1. The Colts are confident Jones will be ready and have awarded him a two-year extension during the offseason. Most of the key pieces of the Colts offense are returning, as wide receivers Alec Pierce (re-signed) and Josh Downs, and tight end Tyler Warren, are back in 2026. With Jones under center again, Taylor is set for another huge season. He currently has an ADP of seventh overall on Sleeper as the third RB off the draft board, which aligns perfectly with RotoBaller's overall ranking of seven. He was one of the safer picks in the back end of the first round of upcoming fantasy football drafts as long as Jones is deemed ready for Week 1.

7.name: James Cook
7.comment: Cook had another fantastic season as the starter for the Bills, finishing fifth overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had nine games with 20-plus fantasy points. Cook led the league in rushing, running for 1,621 yards. He finished with almost 2,000 total yards (1,912) and 14 touchdowns. Cook has three straight 1,000-yard rushing seasons. Cook is a consistent factor in the Bills high-powered offense. Cook has finished 11 or better in fantasy scoring three straight seasons. He has established himself as the Bills lead back and will hold that role for years to come. Cook is a much improved inside runner but does his best work on the outside. He can get to the next level in a hurry. He also is a good pass catcher. Cook also makes plays after contact, averaging an impressive 2.2 yards per carry after contact for his career. He is a complete back.
7.outlook: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III faced plenty of skepticism entering the 2025 season. Fantasy managers questioned whether he could replicate his 18-touchdown total from the year prior, which allowed him to finish as the overall RB8 in PPR leagues. Not only did he repeat his success, but he blew his 2024 fantasy production out of the water. Last season, Cook rushed for 1,621 yards, caught 33 passes for 291 receiving yards, and scored 14 total touchdowns. He played all 17 games, eclipsed 300 fantasy points (PPR) for the first time in his career, and ranked as the overall RB6. Heading into 2026, Cook remains an RB1 with top-five upside at the running back position. His role remains unchanged after the Bills didn't make any major additions to their backfield, and he has shown that he can remain fantasy relevant despite the rushing upside of Josh Allen, who has 100+ rush attempts and 12+ rushing touchdowns in each of the last three years. At the running back position, managers should look for running backs with clear lead-back roles and a good offense. Cook checks both of those boxes, as DraftKings currently has the Bills' line set at 10.5 wins. As long as he stays healthy -- which has not been an issue in the past -- Cook will remain one of the top running backs in fantasy football. As such, he's worth drafting near the middle to end of the first round in 2026 drafts.

8.name: Chase Brown
8.comment: Brown was the starter from day one and had a huge season as the lead back for the Bengals, finishing seventh overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had just three games all season with fewer than double-digit fantasy points. He had 1,456 total yards and 11 touchdowns. Brown had his first 1,000-yard rushing season. He also averaged a solid 2.1 yards per carry after contact, showing he was tough to bring down. Brown has 1,300-plus total yards two straight seasons. He will continue to be the lead back for the Bengals. Brown does his best work between the tackles as a runner. Brown also catches the ball very well and can be an asset out of the backfield as evident by his 54-plus receptions each of the last two seasons. He lacks a little top speed, though, and doesn't make a lot of plays on the outside.
8.outlook: Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown was in danger of falling into bust territory after a slow start to the 2025 season. Brown ended the 2024 campaign on a high note, averaging an elite 20.9 PPR points per game over his last eight games, which pushed him into high-end RB2 territory in 2025 drafts. However, over his first seven games, Brown totaled low 9.8 PPR points per game and averaged just 3.6 YPC. Despite the slow start, Brown would go on to average a much higher 21.2 PPR points per game with 4.8 YPC over his last 10 contests of the campaign to finish the 2025 season as the overall RB7. Much of his early-season struggles were attributed to the absence of Joe Burrow, as the entire offense took a step back without their conductor on the field. Even though Burrow will always carry a high injury risk, when on the field, this Cincinnati offense is among the league's best and can support many high-end fantasy assets. Fortunately for the 26-year-old, the Bengals did not make any major additions to the running back room as veteran Samaje Perine is still slated to operate as his No. 2. With a healthy Burrow and a clear path to a three-down role, Brown has the upside to surpass his RB6 mark from the previous campaign and provide managers with immense value at his current Sleeper ADP of 22 (RB12).

9.name: Omarion Hampton
9.comment: Hampton had injuries limit his rookie year, but he was very productive when on the field. Hampton had 737 total yards and five touchdowns in nine games. If he plays a full season, Hampton has 1,392 total yards, 60 receptions and nine touchdowns. That is a pretty solid rookie season. Hampton had six of nine games with double-digit fantasy points, having at least 13 points all six of those games. If there was a negative, Hampton didn't do much after contact. He averaged just 1.7 yards per carry after contact but did break 15 tackles. Hampton will start from day one in the Chargers offense this year. Hampton is a great fit for the offense. He has power, speed and elusiveness. He can be very tough to bring down. He also is a home-run threat with the ball in his hands, getting downhill in a hurry. Hampton is a legit three-down back.
9.outlook: Los Angeles Chargers running back Omarion Hampton showed flashes of high upside at times during his rookie season but was unable to fully match preseason expectations. Hampton began the season operating as the "1B" in the offense alongside Najee Harris, but after Harris suffered a season-ending Achilles injury in Week 3, Hampton was set up for a heavy workload. Unfortunately, a fractured ankle kept the former North Carolina standout on the shelf for eight straight weeks. However, when on the field, Hampton was quite effective, averaging 15.1 PPR points per game over his first nine NFL contests with a solid 4.4 YPC. He punched in five scores with four of them coming on the ground and was a reliable option in the passing game, drawing 3.9 targets per game. Hampton showed promising underlying metrics, averaging 3.1 yards after contact despite playing behind a Chargers offensive line that was battling several injuries to key contributors. In the offseason, the Chargers added some depth to the backfield with Keaton Mitchell joining Kimani Vidal as the No. 2 and No. 3 options behind the former 22nd overall pick. However, the key factor driving a potential breakout season is the addition of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Even though his time in Miami did not end on a high note, he spearheaded the Miami offense in 2022 and 2023, which finished in the top six in yards and at least the top 11 in total points. This improved play-calling and scheme should help this offense reach a new level in 2026 after averaging a modest 21.6 points per game last fall. While Mitchell and Vidal could occasionally draw opportunities away from Hampton, the 23-year-old projects to see a large workload in one of the game's top offensive units. He is a prime breakout pick going off the boards at pick 17 on Sleeper, making him a low-end RB1 with potential league-winning upside.

10.name: Saquon Barkley
10.comment: Barkley did not follow his career-best season as most hoped. His numbers were way down. He had 1,413 total yards compared to 2,283 the previous season. You have to wonder if all the work in 2024 took it's toll on Barkley last year. He averaged just 4.1 yards per carry and 1.6 yards per carry after contact, his lower total as a pro. He also saw his yards before contact average go way down, showing the offensive line struggles the Eagles had last year. Barkley averaged 2.5 yards before contact compared to 3.8 the previous season. Barkley was just 13th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He just didn't have the big games, topping 20 fantasy points just two games. Barkley has 1,100-plus rushing yards three of four seasons. He will continue to be the focal point of the Eagles offense at age 29. Barkley has great moves in space and can get downhill in a hurry. He is a great runner on the outside but also does well between the tackles. He is a three-down back that can help as a receiver in addition to being a dynamic running back. Barkley can do it all.
10.outlook: Coming off a Super Bowl win and 2K rushing yards in 2024, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley had a solid but unspectacular campaign last year. Barkley rushed for 1,140 yards on 240 rushing attempts and seven touchdowns while catching 33 passes for 278 yards and two scores in 16 games. The 29-year-old didn't show signs of slowing down, with a positive run percentage of 75.7% and a 19.3% broken-tackle percentage. The Eagles' offense struggled for most of last season as quarterback Jalen Hurts and wide receiver A.J. Brown couldn't get on the same page, injuries to the offensive line, and the loss of then-OC Kellen Moore caused Philadelphia's offense to take a step back. In a laundry list of offseason moves, the Eagles traded Brown to the Patriots, drafted USC wide receiver Makai Lemon in the first round, and hired Sean Mannion as their new OC. The Eagles will center their offense behind Barkley again in 2026, but could get backup running back Tank Bigsby more involved, as he was efficient spelling Barkley by averaging 5.9 yards per carry. RotoBaller is projecting Barkley with 1,632 rushing yards on 305 attempts with 12 touchdowns while catching 40 passes in 2026. While the Eagles have shaken things up this year on offense, Barkley should be among the leaders in the NFL in touches and rushing attempts per game, making him a borderline first-round pick in upcoming fantasy football drafts.

11.name: Jeremiyah Love
11.comment: Love was the first running back selected in this year's draft and the third overall player. He heads to the Cardinals to take over as their lead back for years to come. Love is a three-down back capable of helping in both the running and passing game. He has game-changing speed and is a big-play threat every time he has the ball in his hands. He also has good moves in space. Love didn't get a ton of work as a pass catcher in college but has great skills in that area. He isn't really a move the pile back but can run with some power. He should be a huge part of the Cardinals offense from day one.
11.outlook: Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love didn't draw the flashiest landing spot for fantasy football, but as the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, he should be expected to carry a hefty workload in his rookie campaign. The Notre Dame product is one of the best running back prospects in recent memory, and became the first ball carrier selected in the top five since Saquon Barkley in 2018. While it's tough to expect Love to replicate Barkley's rookie season, Barkley is proof that an elite young running back can have league-winning upside in a mid-level NFL offense. Love's $50.5 milliom guarunteed contract ranks first all-time among running backs. Needless to say, the Cardinals didn't draft him to keep him on the sideline. Expect heavy usage and pass-catching volume, as Arizona ranked 10th among all teams last season in total RB receptions. While his mid-second-round ADP makes him far from a smash pick, he has clear top-six RB upside as a homerun hitter with a massive projected workload. Tyler Allgeier, James Conner, and Trey Benson shouldn't scare anyone off selecting Love.

12.name: Josh Jacobs
12.comment: Jacobs wasn't quite as productive in year two with the Packers but still had a solid season, finishing 13th overall in fantasy running back scoring despite missing two games. He did not have a single game hitting the 100-yard rushing mark but all his touchdowns boosted his fantasy value. Jacobs scored 14 total touchdowns. He had five games with 20-plus fantasy points despite not hitting the 100-yard mark. Jacobs should continue to lead the Packers backfield and get a lot of work in that role. Jacobs has 1,000-yard rushing season four of his seven seasons in the NFL. Jacobs has emerged as a top three-down back. Jacobs is a good one-cut back that can get downhill in a hurry. He sets up his blocks well and can get to the next level in a hurry. Jacobs does well in blitz pickup and can get it done in the passing game, having 50-plus catches two of five seasons.
12.outlook: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is expected to remain the team's clear RB1 during the 2026 season, which will provide him with a high workload for fantasy. During the 2025 season, Jacobs punched in at least 13 rushing scores for the second-straight campaign and took 234 attempts (over 15 games) for 929 rushing yards. Through the air, Jacobs caught another 36 passes for 282 yards and a touchdown. The veteran back missed two games of action (with one being Week 18) due to a lingering left knee contusion. While this injury did pave the way for the team's No. 2 option, Emanuel Wilson, to carve out a role behind him, he is now in Seattle, leaving Jacobs as the clear RB1 on the roster, sitting above the unproven Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd. The team did not address this position in the draft as well, leaving the former 24th overall pick as the unquestioned lead back in this offense. However, fantasy managers should continue to monitor his status during training camp, as the running back was arrested and booked on five charges in April, but has since been released from custody. While he appears to have avoided any short-term effects, a potential suspension could still be placed. If Jacobs is clear to suit up in Week 1, fantasy managers should view him as a strong RB1 with top-10 upside at the position. For those looking to target other positions in the opening two rounds, Jacobs provides great value as a high-volume RB1 at his current Sleeper ADP of 26.0, going off the board as the RB13.

13.name: Kenneth Walker III
13.comment: Walker hit the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the first time since his rookie season. He had a career-best 1,309 total yards. He scored just five touchdowns, though, which hurt his fantasy numbers. Walker was just 22nd overall in fantasy running back scoring despite good yardage totals. Walker did play his best football during the Seahawks playoff run, having at least 18 fantasy points all three playoffs games. And Walker won the MVP in the Super Bowl, rushing for a season-high 135 yards. Walker has at least 1,100 total yards three of four seasons. He signed a big deal with the Chiefs this offseason to take over as their starting back. He should play a big role in their offense. Walker is one of the top big-play backs in the game. He can get to the next level in a hurry and is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands. He will try to make a big play too often, losing out on some yards. He is a very good pass catcher that can be an asset in the passing game. Injuries were a concern early in his career but he played a full season last year, which was encouraging.
13.outlook: After being named the MVP of Super Bowl LX while playing for the Seattle Seahawks last season, running back Kenneth Walker III inked a three-year, $43 million contract with the Kansas City Chiefs. Walker III was a productive player during the 2025 regular season as well, recording 1,309 yards from scrimmage and five touchdowns on 252 touches across 17 games. However, his rushing and red zone production were limited by the presence of fellow Seahawks back Zach Charbonnet, who finished the year with 730 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns. In stark contrast, Walker III now profiles as the unencumbered lead back in Kansas City and could have a chance to surpass 17 touches per game for the first time in his NFL career. The quality of the offensive environment around Walker III in Kansas City hinges on the health of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who is currently working his way back from the ACL tear that ended his 2025 campaign. The latest reporting indicates that Mahomes has a chance to be fully cleared by the start of training camp, which would obviously be the best-case scenario for Walker III's fantasy managers. As long as both he and Mahomes stay on the field, Walker III profiles as a solid RB1 with a clear path to posting his most productive fantasy season.

14.name: Javonte Williams
14.comment: A move to Dallas was a great one for Williams, who had his best season to date. He was 11th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He hit the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the first time in his career. Williams had nearly 1,400 total yards and hit double-digit touchdowns (13). He had double-digit fancy points 12 of 17 games. Williams averaged an impressive 4.8 yards per carry. And Williams tied for fifth in yards per carry after contact (2.5 yards). He broke 25 tackles last year, which was the second highest total in football. Williams re-signed with he Cowboys after the season and will continue to serve as their lead back. Williams has 1,000-plus total yards three of five seasons. Williams is a tough back that is hard to bring down. He makes plays after contact and has good moves in space. He can get to the next level in a hurry. He has very good balance after taking a hit. He catches the ball well and can be an asset in the passing game.
14.outlook: It finally came together for Williams last year. We don't think it was a fluke. He can keep it going and might even improve his numbers in year two. Williams is a borderline top-10 fantasy back. Williams can get around 1,500 total yards, 40 receptions and double-digit touchdowns.

15.name: Bucky Irving
15.comment: Irving had an injury-plagued season, missing seven games. He battled ankle and shoulder injuries, and needed shoulder surgery in the offseason to fix the issue. Irving had double-digit fantasy points seven of 10 games. He had 865 total yards. He was limited running the ball, though, averaging just 3.4 yards per carry. Irving also had more than 75-rushing yards just one game all season. Irving really struggled after contact, averaging 1.6 yards per carry after contact after averaging 2.7 his rookie season. This was a big step backwards for him. Irving remains the lead back for the Bucs and hopefully getting back to full strength gets him going again in this offense. Irving is an improving inside runner but really can make plays on the outside because of his top speed. He has proven to be a legit three-down back, having 77 receptions in two seasons. Irving is the complete package at running back and should continue to improve with more seasoning.
15.outlook: Irving is a borderline top-10 fantasy back. Don't let last season deter you too much. He gets plenty of work in the passing game, helping his weekly floor. Irving can get around 1,600 total yards, 50 receptions and double-digit touchdowns.

16.name: Cam Skattebo
16.comment: Skattebo didn't open the season as the starter for the Giants and suffered a terrible injury Week 8, but still managed to finish 37th overall in fantasy running back scoring. Skattebo had double-digit fantasy points all but the first game of the season. Skattebo had 617 total yards and seven touchdowns. If he plays a full year, he has 1,311 total yards, 51 receptions and 15 touchdowns. Skattebo suffered a terrible ankle injury but should be just fine for the start of training camp, having plenty of time to recover. He will start for the Giants from day one this year. Skattebo is a playmaker. He bounces off would-be tacklers, hits the hole in a hurry and can move the pile because of his strength. He also isn't a bad pass catcher and can do well in pass protection. He lacks some top-end speed but that didn't hold him back much his rookie season.
16.outlook: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (ankle) was a pleasant surprise last season as a fourth-round pick for the Giants and eventually surpassed starter Tyrone Tracy Jr. as the team's starting running back. He produced gaudy stats before suffering a gruesome season-ending dislocated ankle in Week 8 against the Eagles. Skattebo rushed for 410 yards on 101 carries with five touchdowns while catching 24 passes for 207 yards and two scores over eight games. He was averaging 15.6 touches per game and proved to be a reliable pass catcher by averaging 8.7 yards after the catch. Some of the Giants' offseason moves include bringing in former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh and drafting OL Francis Mauigoa with the 10th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Skattebo is progressing well from his ankle surgery and participated in 11-on-11 drills during OTAs. He is expected to be a full go for training camp and should have the edge on Tracy as the Giants' starting running back. New York's offense should also be better in quarterback Jaxson Dart's second season as he continues to develop. While Tracy will have a role, the Giants will lean on Skattebo at the goal line, as he owned a terrific 5.0% rushing TD percentage last year. Skattebo is ranked RB20 at RotoBaller and is projected for 1,400 total yards and 11 touchdowns in 2026. Barring a setback, Skattebo is set to be the Giants' workhorse and should produce as an excellent fantasy RB2 if he can stay healthy.

17.name: Breece Hall
17.comment: Hall had a tough season, finishing 19th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had his struggles in a Jets offense that was a disaster much of the year. Hall did have some good games, though, having eight games with double-digit fantasy points. And two of those games he topped 20 fantasy points. Hall hit the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the first time in his career. He averaged 4.4 yards per carry. The big knock on him was a lack of plays after contact, averaging just 1.8 yards per carry after contact. Hall has three straight seasons with at least 1,350 total yards. He has never had double-digit touchdowns for his career, though. Hall can see his production get better in a better offense. He is a very talented back. Hall is the complete package at running back. He has great vision and hits the hole in a hurry. He makes plays in space and has a great hands. Hall can be a top receiving back because of his top route running and hands. He does lack a little thump, though, struggling some after contact throughout his career.
17.outlook: Hall can rebound this year. He has the capabilities to be an elite fantasy back. He should be considered a borderline top-10 fantasy back. Hall can get around 1,500 total yards, 50 receptions and 10 total scores.

18.name: Quinshon Judkins
18.comment: The Browns offense was a mess last year but Judkins was a positive. He looked like the franchise back the Browns hoped to land in last year's draft. He had 998 total yards and seven touchdowns in 14 games. He missed some time because of an ankle injury. Judkins was 16th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had nine of 14 games with double-digit fantasy points, showing good consistency. Judkins did average just 3.6 yards per carry, though, having a hard time finding much room to run. He will be the starter from day one this year and should start for years to come for the Browns. Judkins is a power back that is explosive with the ball in his hands. He can run through tacklers or bounce off of them. He lacks a little wiggle, though. Judkins is a solid pass catcher and willing blocker. He is a solid three-down back.
18.outlook: Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) had an eventful rookie season that, somehow, still left a major imprint in fantasy football. Judkins overcame tribulations stemming from a July arrest related to a domestic violence charge - from which he was cleared - to join Cleveland's backfield in Week 2, and he handled 230 of the Browns' 353 total running back carries despite breaking his leg in Week 15 against the Bills. The team's struggling passing game required Judkins to face a stacked box on a whopping 45.2% of snaps, so his first-glance efficiency metrics don't tell the full story as much as ranking fourth in rushing yards against stacked boxes (356), per NFL's Next Gen Stats. The 22-year-old underwent surgery in late December to address a dislocated right ankle he suffered in Week 16. Cleveland went to work improving its offensive line and wide receiver corps in both free agency and the 2026 NFL Draft, drafting rookie WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, and OL Spencer Fano, creating a better situation for Judkins and whichever Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders gets the nod at quarterback. Likely due to Judkins' positive prognosis for returning to full football activities in June, the Browns did not add a running back despite losing Jerome Ford to Washington in free agency, suggesting the sophomore's monopoly on early-down and goal-line touches should remain, even with a new coach, Todd Monken, calling plays. The running back's sixth-round ADP (63 overall) on Sleeper could be far too late if the offensive improvements manifest in an opportunity to produce double-digit touchdowns, and his role on passing downs could always increase. Dylan Sampson isn't deemed to be as effective in that role as hoped, and Judkins should be the bellcow in Cleveland's offense as long as he's healthy. RotoBaller has Judkins ranked 56th overall, making him a value pick at his current Sleeper ADP.

19.name: Travis Etienne
19.comment: Etienne had a huge season as the top back in the Jaguars offense. He was ninth overall in fantasy running back scoring and finished a yard shy of 1,400 total yards. He had a career high 13 touchdowns. Etienne excelled in the Jaguars new offense under head coach Liam Coen. He was a consistent producer, having 12 games with double-digit fantasy points. Etienne topped 20 points three games. Etienne has 1,000-yard rushing seasons three of four in the NFL. Etienne signed with the Saints to become their top back this season. He is a three-down back that does well as a runner or receiver. Etienne catches the ball very well and can be a big asset in the passing game. He has great moves in space and makes big plays with the ball in his hands. He won't make a ton of plays after contact, though, and can struggle some at times running inside.
19.outlook: Running back Travis Etienne Jr. was one of the top players in the free agent pool this spring and inked a massive four-year, $52 million contract with the emerging New Orleans Saints. After spending the first five seasons of his NFL career with the Jaguars, Etienne is set to operate as the lead running back on a Saints team that hopes to take a step forward in 2026. Following a down season in 2024, when Etienne ran for a career-low 558 rushing yards and just two touchdowns, the running back bounced back in a big way in 2025. Entering the season, the former Clemson standout was not guaranteed the starting job, but quickly reclaimed the role, totaling 1,107 yards on the ground, the second-highest mark of his career, and adding seven rushing scores. Through the air, Etienne brought in another 36 catches (52 targets) for 292 yards and another six touchdowns. Last season, the Saints' major weakness was their rushing attack, as veteran Alvin Kamara struggled to find much traction, and the team posted the 10th-fewest rushing yards per game. As a result, the team views Etienne as not only the future of the backfield but also the answer to this short-term weakness. While Kamara is still on the roster, Etienne figures to operate as the lead option with the veteran reverting to a change-of-pace role. Given that young quarterback Tyler Shough averaged a strong 260.0 passing yards per game over his last eight games, this offense could take a massive step forward with a stable rushing game. Etienne carries surprising value as a high-end RB2 despite his newly signed contract, as he is being selected as the RB18 in current PPR Sleeper drafts at an ADP of 39.0. Etienne should contend for another double-digit touchdown campaign while seeing ample targets, making him one of the best values among RB2s on the draft board.

20.name: Kyren Williams
20.comment: Williams split a little more work at running back with Blake Corum emerging, but that didn't slow Williams from having another big season. He was eighth overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had double-digit fantasy points all but two games, showing remarkable consistency. Williams had a career high in total yards, finishing with 1,533 total yards. He also scored 13 touchdowns, giving him three straight seasons with 1,300-plus total yards and double-digit scores. Williams will continue to be the top back in this Rams explosive offense but should cede some carries to Corum once again. Williams is a top three-down back. He catches the ball well and also can carry the load at running back. He makes plays after contact and has enough speed to make the big play.
20.outlook: Los Angeles Rams Kyren Williams has served as the lead back in one of the game's most consistent offenses since his second season in the NFL (2023). From 2023 through 2025, the former Notre Dame standout has punched in double-digit rushing scores in each campaign, totaling at least 1,100 rushing yards in each season. He has been highly involved in the passing game as well, catching at least 30 passes in each season. While Williams opened the 2025 season as a clear workhorse as expected, his usage began to drop in the second half following the emergence of Blake Corum. From Weeks 1 through 9, Williams looked like his typical self, taking 16.5 attempts per game while drawing 3.3 targets per game. However, from Weeks 10 through 17, Williams would take 14.5 attempts per game with 2.4 targets per game. During this eight-game stretch, much of his workload was skewed by an outlier 23-carry game in Week 16. In this noted stretch, Corum took 10.1 rushing attempts per game. While Williams remains the "1A" in this backfield, Corum is beginning to close the gap, which will drastically lower Williams' floor. While the Los Angeles offense projects to be as potent as it was in 2025 with the return of Matthew Stafford, Williams could fall into the low-end RB1 tier with a smaller workload. Managers have already begun pushing the 25-year-old down early draft boards as he is going off the board as the RB17 (36.0 ADP) on Sleeper, making him an intriguing value play for those who trust his ability to find the back of the end zone. However, there is still inherent risk in this selection, even at a lower cost, as a large role for Corum could make Williams a mid-end RB2 on a weekly basis in 2026.

21.name: Derrick Henry
21.comment: Henry just keeps getting it done, having another big season as the Ravens lead back. The offense had more struggles with Lamar Jackson banged up, but that didn't slow Henry much. He was eighth overall in fantasy running back scoring and ran for nearly 1,600 yards. He also had 16-rushing touchdowns for the second straight season. Henry averaged an impressive 5.2 yards per carry, which is pretty unheard of for a running back of his age. He continues to make plays after contact, averaging 2.4 yards per carry after contact. Henry also averaged 2.8 yards per carry before contact, showing he runs behind a great offensive line and can do well making defenders miss. You have to think Henry will slow down at some point but it is hard to count him out. He will be 32 years old this coming season. Henry is a great one-cut runner that can get downhill in a hurry. Henry can be a punishing runner. He lacks some moves in space, but makes up for that with his running style and top speed. Henry doesn't get much work as a receiver, having fewer than 20 receptions all but two years.
21.outlook: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry's 2025 season wasn't quite as prolific as his 2024 campaign, when he topped 2,100 scrimmage yards and finished fourth in the AP Offensive Player of the Year voting. Still, the ageless wonder recorded 1,595 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns on 307 carries across 17 games. Henry has now recorded double-digit rushing touchdowns in eight consecutive seasons, and he's averaged 5.6 yards across his first two years with the Ravens. Henry is entering his age-32 season in 2026 and is on pace to become just the 21st player in NFL history to reach 3,000 career touches, which naturally leads to questions around when he will start to decline. The veteran back has also recorded just 34 receptions on 43 touches across his 34 career games with Baltimore, so his fantasy production is heavily reliant on both high-volume and high-efficiency rushing. At the same time, it's difficult to bet against Henry when he's been such a reliable force and remained extremely effective in 2025. He also should spend more time playing in a fully operational Baltimore offense in 2026 after star Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missed four games last season due to injury. Fantasy managers will have to weigh the possibility of age-related decline when selecting Henry, but he projects as a low-end fantasy RB1 entering his 11th NFL season.

22.name: TreVeyon Henderson
22.comment: Henderson had a solid rookie season. He was 21st overall in fantasy running back scoring despite playing a reserve role much of the year. Henderson had 1,132 total yards and 10 touchdowns. He averaged an impressive 5.1 yards per carry. Henderson had nine games with double-digit fantasy points. Henderson should play a big role for the Patriots once again this year. He might not start but should at least split the work for the team. Henderson is one of the top big-play backs in the game. He will struggle a little running on the inside but should improve on that with more seasoning. Henderson can make a ton of plays on the outside and is an improving pass catcher. Henderson can develop into a top three-down back in time. He will need improve his blocking if he hopes to have that role, though.
22.outlook: In his rookie season, New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson's role in New England's offense was limited to start the year. Henderson averaged just 6.1 rushing attempts in the team's first seven games of the season. The usage to start the year was puzzling, as Henderson was arguably the team's most explosive playmaker. New England finally let Henderson loose in Week 8, and the Ohio State product rushed for 758 yards on 137 attempts while catching 19 passes for 122 yards over the team's final 10 games. Overall, Henderson took advantage of an easy schedule, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, racking up 10 scores on 215 touches, including four from 50-plus yards. It was an even split with Rhamondre Stevenson, but the team leaned more on Rhambo in the playoffs, as he had 17.8 touches compared to Henderson's 8.8. Henderson will look to carve out a role in a high-octane Patriots offense as the team added wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason. The 23-year-old has an injury history at Ohio State and expect the Pats to utilize Henderson as they did last year to keep him healthy. Henderson has the potential to be a fantasy RB1 if Stevenson goes down or is benched, but expect the second-year back to see spike weeks with the backfield split. Henderson is currently RB22 in the latest RotoBaller rankings with a Sleeper ADP of 48, making him a solid pick in the middle rounds. However, with a tougher schedule and some expected spike weeks, Henderson is a better pick in best ball formats.

23.name: David Montgomery
23.comment: The Lions didn't have quite the split in the backfield as the previous few seasons, giving Montgomery a few less chances. He had 908 total yards and eight touchdowns. Montgomery was 27th overall in fantasy running back scoring, having double-digit fantasy points seven games. It wasn't all bad for him, averaging 4.5 yards per carry, which was up from the previous year. He has been a very productive back through the years and does well in a split backfield, which could be the case for him again this year. He heads to the Texans to likely serve as their No. 1 back but should lose out on some work to second-year back Woody Mark. Montgomery is likely to get a few more touches than he has the last few years in Detroit, though. Montgomery is a good between the tackles runner. He is a big back that runs with power and does well after contact. He also is a solid receiver that can make plays in the passing game when given the chance. He lacks a little elusiveness, though, but will make some plays in space. He also is one of the better short-yardage backs in the game.
23.outlook: After three successful seasons with the Detroit Lions, the Houston Texans acquired running back David Montgomery for a fourth and sixth-round pick, and he's now in a position to see his largest workload in years. The Nick Chubb experiment failed in Houston, and out of necessity, 2025 fourth-round pick Woody Marks led the team in carries. Marks was not overly efficient with the opportunities given, averaging only 3.6 yards per carry, and he should fall back into a more natural pass-catching role in 2026. Though even as a change-of-pace back, he does not possess the sort of game-breaking ability to regularly take snaps away from Montgomery. Montgomery spent his time in Detroit sharing a backfield with former first-round pick Jahmyr Gibbs, who eventually took the leap to superstar status in year three, limiting Montgomery to the fewest carries of his career, despite playing all 17 games in 2025. While his raw numbers were down as a result, his efficiency was not. Montgomery's 3.17 yards after contact per carry in 2025 marked a career high, and even while his three-time Pro Bowl running mate was piling up accolades, Montgomery managed to average 230 touches, 1,137 yards, and nearly a dozen touchdowns across his three seasons as a Lion. As RotoBaller's RB22, he is one of the more mispriced running backs in this year's dead zone, and with a clear path to a bellcow role on a team built to play with a lead, a healthy Montgomery could handsomely reward drafters willing to wait on the position.

24.name: Bhayshul Tuten
24.comment: Tuten earned the top backup job for the Jaguars his rookie season. He didn't play a ton in that role but showed well with his chances. Tuten had 386 total yards and seven touchdowns. He could play a bigger role for the coming season, splitting more of the work at running back or even starting. Tuten has big-time speed, getting to the next level in a hurry. He lacks some size, though, and fumbling can be an issue. He shows well as a three-down back and could grow into the role sooner than later.
24.outlook: After being drafted in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten finished his rookie season with 386 yards from scrimmage and seven touchdowns on 93 touches across 15 games. The 23-year-old flashed high-end upside throughout the year, but he was ultimately blocked from fantasy-relevant production by the presence of former Jaguars running back Travis Etienne Jr. Entering 2026, Etienne Jr. is no longer in Jacksonville after signing a big-money free agent contract with the New Orleans Saints. As a result, Tuten could be poised to emerge as the new lead back for the Jaguars. Jacksonville did make a move in free agency to fortify its backfield after losing Etienne Jr. by signing former Washington Commanders running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. Rodriguez Jr. rushed for 500 yards and six touchdowns on 112 carries in 2025 and could steal touches away from Tuten. Still, Tuten profiles as the higher-upside back and enters the year with the advantage of experience in Jaguars play-caller Liam Coen's system. If Tuten can seize the majority of the backfield work in Jacksonville, he could be on the verge of a breakout season. RotoBaller ranks Tuten as its RB23 entering 2026.

25.name: RJ Harvey
25.comment: Harvey emerged as the starter for the Broncos his rookie season, starting seven games. He was 20th overall in fantasy scoring, mainly because of his touchdown totals. Harvey scored 12 touchdowns. He had 896 total yards and 47 receptions. Harvey had 18-plus fantasy points four of his last six games. Harvey did average just 3.7 yards per carry, which wasn't great. And he didn't make many plays after contact, averaging 1.8 per carry after contact. Harvey will need to improve in both areas if hopes to be a three-down back in the NFL. For now, he is likely to split work with JK Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman in the Broncos backfield. Harvey is a smaller back but runs with patience and can get to the next level in a hurry. He has great wiggle and is a home-run threat from anywhere on the field. Harvey also catches the ball well as evident by his 47 receptions last year.
25.outlook: Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey stepped up as a rookie, notching 12 total touchdowns with 146 carries for 540 rushing yards alongside another 356 yards through the air on 47 catches. Even before J.K. Dobbins was lost for the year to a foot injury, Harvey had scored six TDs on 75 touches through 10 weeks, operating as a change-of-pace back. After Dobbins went down, Harvey tallied 96-326-5 on the ground (3.4 YPC) with another 22-181-1 receiving, so we saw more volume rather than big plays. But this did result in four top-12 RB weeks (half-PPR) between Weeks 13-17. He then tore his labrum in the AFC Championship Round and required shoulder surgery, which has limited his offseason involvement. Dobbins is now healthy, and Denver also took Jonah Coleman in the fourth round, so there's pessimism around the sophomore RB who relied on volume and TDs to pop. He may slide from his June half-PPR ADP of the RB30, going around overall pick 80, as a result. Our RotoBaller ranks have him closer to pick 90.

26.name: Jadarian Price
26.comment: The Seahawks took Price with the last pick in the first round, hoping to have found their replacement for Kenneth Walker in the offense. Price has a chance to start from day on his rookie season with Zach Charbonnet returning from a major injury. Price is a good one-cut runner. He can get to the next level in a hurry and has good instincts for the position. He is good in short-yardage situations and had a knack for finding the end zone in college. He has little experience as a pass catcher, though, so that could be an issue early in his career. Price has the talent to become a top three-down back in the NFL, but it might take a few years for that to happen.
26.outlook: When looking at running backs with the potential to make an impact as rookies, the list is Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price; that's it. That's the list. Seattle used the final pick of the first round to select Price, as the Seahawks run game entered uncertain waters heading into the 2026 season with Kenneth Walker III's departure and Zach Charbonnet recovering from a late-season ACL injury. Between Walker and Charbonnet, Seattle ran the ball 405 times last season, meaning Price will be in line for a heavy workload, especially early on in the season. As for fantasy, both Walker and Charbonnet averaged 11.3 fantasy points per game, which tells us that Price has one of the highest floors, not only as far as rookies are concerned, but looking at the running back position, there is enough production to lead to finishing as a top-10 fantasy option at the position. The math suggests that Seattle's run game will produce 22.6 fantasy points per game, and with Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani as the only healthy running backs available, Price could be in line to repeat Walker's playoff production. In three playoff games, Walker had 65 rushing attempts resulting in 313 rushing yards and four touchdowns. Add that up, and you have 18.4 fantasy points per game without including the nine receptions for 104 yards.

27.name: Rico Dowdle
27.comment: Dowdle had a solid first season with the Panthers, starting much of the year. He hit the 1,000-yard mark for the second straight season and finished 17th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had nine games with double-digit fantasy points, including two games with 30-plus points. Dowdle took a backseat some late in the year, though, failing to hit double-digit carries three of his last four games. It was a poor finish for Dowdle. He did average a solid 4.6 yards per carry and 2.0 yards per carry after contact. Dowdle signed with the Steelers and could be in a similar situation to last year, splitting some work with Jaylen Warren. Dowdle runs with some power and has pretty good moves in space. He lacks a little top speed but does well in churning out the yards. He also is a solid pass catcher as evident by his 39 receptions each of the last two seasons.
27.outlook: Rico Dowdle is going for the trifecta, usurping a starting running back for the third time in as many years. The formerly undrafted runner first got his chance in Dallas in 2024, replacing the aging and ineffective Ezekiel Elliott. That led to a one-year contract with Carolina, where he outproduced Chuba Hubbard (for part of the season anyway) and became a fantasy football sensation with consecutive games of over 230 scrimmage yards. After back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons, Dowdle is now a Pittsburgh Steeler and reunited with head coach Mike McCarthy for another complementary role. Albeit a different type of running back, Dowdle replaces the outgoing Kenneth Gainwell to play the 1B role to Jaylen Warren, with the latter getting the edge in the receiving department. Given his past success, Dowdle ranks as one of the best insurance running backs in fantasy football in 2026 and could hold weekly standalone flex value.

28.name: D'Andre Swift
28.comment: Swift hit the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the second time in his career last year. He was 15th overall in fantasy running back scoring. Swift had 11 of 17 games with double-digit fantasy points, showing great consistency. He had a productive season in the Bears new offense and seemed a good fit for the scheme. Swift did end up splitting more work late in the year with rookie Kyle Monangai, which is likely to be a trend going forward. Swift has two straight seasons with 1,300 plus total yards. Swift is a powerful back with top speed. He can get to the next level in a hurry. Swift is tough to bring down in the open field. Swift will drop some passes but is a very capable route runner and three-down back. Injuries are always a concern with Swift, but he was much better in that area the last three seasons.
28.outlook: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift had a career year under first-time head coach Ben Johnson. Swift rushed for 1,087 yards on 223 rushing attempts and nine touchdowns while catching 34 passes for 299 yards and a score over 16 games last season. The 27-year-old also averaged 16.1 touches per game while averaging 2.9 yards after contact. He did split touches with backfield teammate Kyle Monangai. However, the two formed a solid duo and elevated the Bears' rushing attack, as the team averaged 144.5 rushing yards per game, third-best in the NFL. Chicago did not sign or draft a running back this offseason and will roll with the Swift/Monangai combination again in 2026. The Bears o-line should be solid again, and quarterback Caleb Williams will look to build on his excellent sophomore season. Swift is entering the final year of this three-year contract with the Bears and should continue to see plenty of usage to remain a solid fantasy RB2. He is currently ranked as RB19 in the latest RotoBaller rankings and is projected to rack up 1,332 yards from scrimmage with 32 receptions and nine touchdowns in 2026. Despite Monangai being the Bears closer and taking some touches away, Swift is a solid mid-round pick heading into upcoming fantasy football drafts.

29.name: Jaylen Warren
29.comment: Warren had the best season of his career, finishing 18th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had 1,291 total yards and eight touchdowns. He also ran for 958 yards. All three of those totals were career highs for Warren. He had 11 of 16 games with double-digit fantasy points. It was the first season he was the full-time starter and Warren showed he can play that role well. And although he isn't the biggest back, Warren ran with some power, averaging 2.4 yards per carry after contact. Warren has more competition for carries this year with Rico Dowdle now in the mix. Warren could play more of a third-down role with Dowdle getting the early-down work. Warren is a very fast back. He can make plays after contact, though, and also is tough to bring down in the open field because of his top speed. He can get to the next level in a hurry. Warren hits the hole in a hurry and catches the ball well, making him a solid three-down back.
29.outlook: Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren has outperformed ADP in three of his first four seasons in the league, and coming into 2026 as RotoBaller's RB32, he has a solid chance of improving upon that trend. Since signing on with Pittsburgh as an undrafted free agent in 2022, Warren has proven himself to be one of the most well-rounded, underrated backs in the league. In two of his three seasons sharing the backfield with former first-round pick Najee Harris, he topped 160 opportunities, and he never fell below 5.2 yards per touch. Last year, as Kenneth Gainwell racked up the fourth most running back receptions in the league, Warren was not far behind with 40 of his own, while his 1.58 yards per route run ranked sixth among qualified backs. The Steelers added Rico Dowdle in free agency, and while he was able to top 1,000 yards at each of his last two stops in Carolina and Dallas, he has never handled a bellcow role for an extended stretch. He also doesn't possess any single trait to justify Warren's fall to the back of the seventh round after an RB16 finish in 2025. At 215 pounds, Dowdle's 236 carries in 2025 do not come close to the workload of a prime Harris, and his career-high 39 receptions came while sharing the backfield with one of the league's most inefficient pass catchers in Chuba Hubbard. Warren has fended off larger threats while finishing as a top-25 back in two of his last three seasons. While he may not offer the league-winning upside that some drafters prefer to swing for from the later rounds, Warren is a safe bet to return value, and he has a proven track record of thriving under similar circumstances.

30.name: Kyle Monangai
30.comment: Monangai had a really impressive rookie season, finishing just shy of 1,000 total yards. He was 30th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had six games with double-digit fantasy points. Monangai started the season in a reserve role but was almost splitting the work with D'Andre Swift by season's end. Expect Monangai to have a role in this offense from day one this year. He is a small back but runs with some power and can do well as a pass catcher out of the backfield. Monangai has good moves in space and can get to the outside in a hurry.
30.outlook: Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai is entering Year 2 with a chance to take a huge step forward. Monangai's role within Chicago's offense grew as the 2025 season wore on, culminating in 783 rushing yards and five touchdowns. He brought a combination of explosion and power that the Bears' offense needed. In Year 2 of head coach Ben Johnson's system, Monangai's role should only continue to grow. As the 2025 season progressed, the Bears' running back tandem of Monangai and D'Andre Swift was beginning to look like the Jahmyr Gibbs-David Montgomery combination we saw during Johnson's Detroit days. The difference here is that Monangai is a more explosive player than his counterpart, Montgomery. While Monangai seems poised to begin the season in the backup role once again, there is a real possibility that he works his way into the starting role at some point. At minimum, Monangai is well-positioned for something close to a 50/50 timeshare. After finishing as the RB30 in 2025, Monangai is being drafted in that range early in the draft process. He is absolutely worth that price, with a legitimate chance to finish in the top 24.

31.name: J.K. Dobbins
31.comment: Dobbins won the starting job in Denver before the season and ran well in that role before suffering a foot injury that ended his season early. He had 809 total yards in 10 games before getting hurt. He averaged an impressive 5.0 yards per carry and had double-digit fantasy points five straight games to start his season. Dobbins was tough to bring down, averaging 2.4 yards per carry after contact. Dobbins continues to struggle with injury, though. He has yet to play a full season in the NFL and has played 47 games in six seasons. If healthy, Dobbins is likely to be the top back for the Broncos but could split a little more work with RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman. Dobbins is a strong back that does his best work between the tackles. He is tough to bring down because of his size and strength. Dobbins is an improved pass catcher, having 52 receptions his past two seasons. He has become a more complete back.
31.outlook: J.K. Dobbins secured a two-year, $16 million contract with the Broncos in March. That provides the 27-year-old Dobbins with a navigable path toward reclaiming the early-down role that he seized during 2025. All concerns surrounding Dobbins' track record of health issues are justified. However, he is positioned to operate as the lead back in Sean Payton's offense while he remains unencumbered by injuries. Dobbins performed effectively in that role last season, while finishing among the top five in attempts (153/15.3 per game) and rushing yards (772/77.2 per game) from Weeks 1-10. He was also eighth among backs with 100+ carries in missed tackles forced per attempt (0.20) per Fantasy Points Data. Dobbins also sustained a season-ending foot injury in Week 10, which halted his statistical momentum. RJ Harvey vaulted to ninth among backs in targets (29/4.1 per game) and receptions (22/3.1 per game), while tying for fifth in rushing touchdowns (five) during Dobbins' absence. However, Harvey failed to surpass 3.4 yards per attempt in five of his seven games during that sequence. He also finished 51st in efficiency (4.85) from Weeks 1-18 per Next Gen Stats. Harvey's inefficiency reduces his prospects of securing an expanded workload as a rusher, but he should function as the backfield's primary pass-catcher. Fourth-round selection Jonah Coleman should also accumulate carries and targets as his rookie season progresses. That will not impact Dobbins' role as Denver's lead rusher, provided that he can avoid additional injuries. This supplies your incentive to pursue Dobbins near his Round 9 ADP in best-ball drafts (104/RB35) and his Round 10 ADP in dynasty startups (119/RB39).

32.name: Tony Pollard
32.comment: Pollard hit the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the fourth straight season. He was 23rd overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had 100-yard games three of his last five to end his season, playing his best football late in the season. Pollard had double-digit fantasy points eight of 17 games. He posted pretty consistent numbers as the Titans starter once again. Pollard might be moved to more of a split backfield going froward, though. He can serve that role well, having done so at previous stops. Pollard is effective as a runner or receiver. He does well in space and can get downfield in a hurry. He is a big-play threat at the position. Pollard also is an improved inside runner. He does lack a little size but has been able to carry the load without issue in recent seasons.
32.outlook: Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard has quietly remained one of the more reliable fantasy backs in the league, topping 1,000 rushing yards and 30 receptions in each of the past four seasons while never finishing worse than RB24 in half-PPR formats. Despite that consistency, the 29-year-old former Pro Bowler has fallen well into this year's running back dead zone, sliding to RB30 in RotoBaller's 2026 redraft rankings. Tennessee spent a fifth-round pick on running back Nicholas Singleton, adding a degree of competition to the Titans' backfield. While a broken foot suffered at the 2026 Senior Bowl likely contributed to his slide into Day 3, his fall from one of the top high school recruits in the nation also suggests an inability to shake some of the concerns about his poor vision and stiffness, potentially making him more of a developmental project than an immediate threat to Pollard's workload. New offensive coordinator Brian Daboll should prove capable of boosting a Titans offense that averaged 232 total yards under Brian Callahan but showed signs of growth after his Week 7 firing. Following Daboll from the Giants is wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson, and the team spent the fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft on Ohio State's Carnell Tate, but even if the Titans don't take a monumental step forward on offense, Pollard projects once again as a steady RB2 option. His all-around skill set makes him the favorite to remain the lead back, with weekly volume and receiving usage capable of keeping his fantasy floor intact.

33.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
33.comment: Stevenson missed some time because of injury but started most of the year for the Patriots high-powered offense. He had 948 total yards and nine touchdowns in 14 games, finishing 25h overall in fantasy running back scoring. He played his beset football late in the season, having 17-plus fantasy points three straight games to end his season. Stevenson rebounded from a ho-hum season the previous year. He averaged 4.6 yards per carry and over 10 yards per receptions. And Stevenson was hard to bring down, averaging 2.8 yards per carry after contact. This was the second best total in football. Stevenson played more than rookie Tre'Veyon Henderson last year but that could change some this year. Stevenson should still play a big role offensively but likely loses more touches. Stevenson has 1,000-plus total yards one of five seasons. Stevenson does well between the tackles and is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands. He makes plays after contact and has enough speed to make plays on the outside. He lacks some elusiveness, but can make up with that because of his size and speed. He also catches the ball well and is a legit three-down back.
33.outlook: New England Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson was solid for fantasy managers in a split backfield last season. He rushed for 603 yards on 130 attempts while catching 32 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns in 14 games. The 28-year-old averaged 4.6 yards per carry and gained positive yardage 77.7% of the time. The Patriots leaned more on Stevenson over TreVeyon Henderson in the playoffs, as he had 17.8 touches compared to Henderson's 8.8. New England's offense should be explosive again heading into 2026 as the Patriots added wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason. Stevenson will need to hold onto the ball if he plans to fend off Henderson for touches, as Rhambo has fumbled the ball 10 times over his last 20 games. The good news is he didn't fumble from Week 5 on last year after dropping the ball three times in the team's first five weeks. With the split backfield, Stevenson is more of a high-end FLEX play each week and is currently RB28 in the latest RotoBaller rankings. The touches in the playoffs suggest Stevenson should have a small edge over more elusive Henderson, but that quickly changes if he starts fumbling again. Rhambo is projected for 1,079 total yards and nine touchdowns, making him a decent pick at his current 75 ADP at Sleeper.

34.name: Jordan Mason
34.comment: Mason had a solid first season in Minnesota, splitting the work tie Aaron Jones many weeks. He had 809 total yards and a career-high six touchdowns. Mason was 36th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had double-digit fantasy points six games. Mason averaged a very impressive 4.8 yards per carry. Mason also did well after contact, averaging 2.4 yards per array after contact. He broke 13 tackles running the ball. He is likely to split work again at running back for Minnesota this year but might get a few more touches and serve as more of the lead back. Mason is a tough insider runner that does well after contact. He is getting better at catching the ball but that isn't a strength of his play. He has 800-plus total yards two straight seasons.
34.outlook: Minnesota Vikings running back Jordan Mason remains the second RB on his team's depth chart. Aaron Jones is still the starter, and though his advanced age and proneness to injury could create more opportunity for Mason, the Vikings drafted rookie Demond Claiborne to compete for the backup job. Outside of one game in Week 3 against one of the league's worst rush defenses, Mason was disappointing in 2025, and failed to take the starting job from Jones despite plenty of opportunity. The backup lacks pass-catching upside and averaged under four yards per carry aside from Week 3 in games where he had 10 or more carries. Claiborne will probably get worked into the offense as a rusher while Jones handles the majority of the work and most of the pass-catching downs. Fantasy managers looking for a high-upside handcuff should look away from Mason in 2026.

35.name: Rachaad White
35.comment: White saw his playing time decrease once again last year, rushing 132 times for 572 yards and four touchdowns. He had 790 total yards, failing to hit 1,000 yards for the first time since his rookie season. White was 32nd overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had four games with double-digit fantasy points, but failed to hit that mark after Week 10. White averaged just 1.5 yards per carry after contact, struggling to do much after getting hit. This has been an issues for him throughout his career, though. White will look to get things going again this year after signing with the Commanders. He will look to earn the top backup role with his new team. White has 40 or more receptions all four seasons in the NFL. He can serve the change-of-pace role well. White does a good job of setting blocks and making plays in the passing game. White lacks a little explosiveness, though, and breakaway speed. He also has not been good after contact throughout his NFL career.
35.outlook: Rachaad White surrendered the starting running back role in Tampa Bay largely due to rushing inefficiencies. That's not the strong suit of his game, with a career average of 3.9 yards per carry. What he lacks on the ground, he makes up for through the air, catching at least 40 passes in every season in Central Florida. Now a member of the Washington Commanders and reunited with his college quarterback, Jayden Daniels, White doesn't have to look over his shoulder at more capable running backs behind him. Seventh-round sophomore Jacory Croskey-Merritt, sixth-round rookie Kaytron Allen, and Jerome Ford round out the depth chart. At worst, White excels in the third-down and pass-catching roles. More likely, he's getting the bulk of the touches for an offense that should rebound with a healthy Daniels. He is, after all, just a few seasons removed from the RB4 finish in PPR leagues.

36.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
36.comment: Croskey-Merritt had an unexpected rookie season. He ended up starting much of the season and had 873 total yards and eight touchdowns. He was 33rd overall in fantasy running back scoring. Croskey-Merritt had five games with double-digit fantasy points, including two games with 20-plus points. He had plenty of chances to run away with the starting job but couldn't. He showed enough to earn a role on a weekly basis for the coming season, though. Croskey-Merritt averaged 4.6 yards per carry and 2.1 yards per carry after contact. He is a speed back but showed well after contact, running with some power. He isn't much of a pass catcher at this stage of his career, catching just nine passes last season.
36.outlook: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is flying under the radar this offseason, which is the polar opposite of the hype he was receiving a year ago. Croskey-Merritt underperformed as a rookie despite rushing for 805 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries. That is solid production, especially for the situation Croskey-Merritt was put in. He was a 7th-round pick who was forced to sit out his final year of college due to an NCAA clerical error regarding his freshman year at Alabama State. Additionally, Croskey-Merritt was forced to be a focal point of the Commanders' offense after Jayden Daniels and Terry McLaurin battled injuries all season. In 2026, his situation has drastically improved with Daniels healthy, an improved offensive line, and a new offense that favors his running style. The Commanders did not acquire a big-name running back this offseason, which highlights their faith in Croskey-Merritt to take his game to another level. Croskey-Merritt can take his biggest fantasy jump with his touchdown production. Similar to James Cook's situation in Buffalo, there is no overwhelming red zone threat through the air in the Commanders' offense. This gives Croskey-Merritt a clear path to hit double-digit touchdowns this season in an offense with lofty expectations. Croskey-Merritt is currently being drafted as an RB4 despite having achievable RB2 upside. After a full season back in football and being in a better offensive ecosystem, Croskey-Merritt is in a better position to live up to those high expectations from last season.

37.name: Woody Marks
37.comment: Marks became the starter for the Texans his rookie season. He finished 29th overall in fantasy running back scoring. Marks had 911 total yards and five touchdowns.
