Marks had six of 16 games with double-digit fantasy points. He did average just 3.6 yards per carry, though, and 1.8 yards per carry after contact. Both those numbers weren't too impressive. The Texans went out and got David Montgomery this offseason. He should become the No. 1 back with Marks backing him up. Marks lacks a little speed and moves in space, but does well in churning out the yards and can make plays after contact. He also is a decent pass catcher, showing three-down ability.
37.outlook: Houston Texans running back Woody Marks pushed through weekly bumps and bruises to turn 196 carries into 703 yards and two touchdowns, with another three scores and 208 yards on 24 catches. It was a lost season for Joe Mixon (foot), which led to Marks splitting time with Nick Chubb throughout the first half of the season and popping onto fantasy radars as the PPR RB6 in Week 4 (27.9 points). But he never scored more than 16.1 PPR points for us again, as more volume behind a poor line led to a meager 3.6 yards per carry. On top of that, his 0.06 missed tackles forced per attempt was tied for the worst mark out of 49 RBs who saw more than 100 carries. So he wasn't breaking many tackles, and his 1.59 yards before contact per attempt was 44th. In short, he had little room to operate, and couldn't create many new opportunities for himself. And the Texans brought in David Montgomery, who should absorb much of the valuable goal-line work and played all 17 games last year, relegating Marks to pass-catching spellback duties. A strong defense could mean fewer garbage-time passing theaters as well, if we're becoming more reliant on that avenue. For now, Marks' half-PPR RotoBaller rank and ADP are aligned at RB45 near pick 140 overall, making him a fine zero or hero-RB target after building strength elsewhere in your lineup.

38.name: Chuba Hubbard
38.comment: Hubbard had a disappointing season, losing out on his starter's job to Rico Dowdle. Hubbard had 734 total yards in 15 games, including six starts. He was 42nd overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had double-digit fantasy points each of his first two games but didn't reach that mark again the rest of the season. Hubbard averaged just 3.8 yards per carry and broke just one tackle all season running the ball. His lack of plays after contact really hurt his production. Hubbard is likely stuck in a platoon role once again this year in Carolina. Hubbard had two straight seasons with 1,100-plus total yards before last year. Hubbard has very good vision and does a good job of setting his blocks. Hubbard lacks a little size for the position but that hasn't slowed him a whole lot. He is a much improved pass catcher and can do well as a three-down back.
38.outlook: Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard suffered a calf injury in Week 4 against the New England Patriots and ended up missing the next two weeks. He returned to action in Week 7, but took a backseat to Rico Dowdle and only logged double-digit carries three times in the Panthers' last 12 games, including the Wild Card loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Overall, Hubbard rushed for 511 yards on 134 attempts and one touchdown while catching 30 passes for 223 yards and three scores across 15 games. Dowdle left via free agency and signed a two-year, $12.5 million contract with the Steelers. Part of the reason the Panthers let Dowdle walk is that the team feels running back Jonathon Brooks (knee) is healthy and ready to take on a role in Carolina's backfield. Brooks missed all of last season after suffering a torn ACL in his rookie year. The 22-year-old appears to be fully healthy and has looked impressive in OTAs. While Brooks will have a role, the Panthers could ease him in and rely on Hubbard to lead the Panthers' backfield. Hubbard has an ADP of 91 on Sleeper, and is massive value with a current RotoBaller ranking of 67. If Hubbard can fend off Brooks, he's an excellent pick at his current ADP. RotoBaller projections have Hubbard leading the backfield, projecting 1,270 total yards and eight touchdowns in 2026.

39.name: Tyjae Spears
39.comment: Spears was the clear backup to Tony Pollard and had double-digit carries just one game all season. He had 547 total yards and two touchdowns in 13 games. Spears had two games with double-digit fantasy points. Spears got more work as a pass catcher than runner, having 45 receptions. He has been more of a third-down back throughout his career and likely serves that role once again this year. Spears can get to the next level in a hurry, showing some of the best speed of any running back in the game. He has great speed for the position and does well in the open field. He lacks a little power, though, and can struggle to churn out the tough yards. Spears is a good pass catcher and can be a huge asset in the passing game.
39.outlook: Tennessee Titans running back Tyjae Spears continued to be a solid receiving option out of the backfield in 2025, though he still underwhelmed as a rusher. He brought in 45 of 50 targets for 264 yards in the air while gaining 283 yards on 72 carries (3.9 YPC) with two ground scores, with Tony Pollard seeing 275 touches for 1,288 total yards as the alpha. Though there's little reason to believe that Pollard will cede more work after strong results, Spears could've been hampered by a high-ankle sprain suffered in the preseason that forced him to the injured reserve to open the season. And with Pollard not missing any time, we saw Spears orbit a weekly 45-55% snap rate, finishing with two PPR top-12 weeks and another seven in the RB21-RB37 range as a fine flex play. However, the team did draft Nicholas Singleton in the fifth round, who got more involved as a receiver at Penn State as he progressed, though pass protection remains a liability until proven otherwise. As such, Spears should have a decent chance at maintaining this low-ceiling PPR role as a later pick near the 155 ADP right by the edge of RotoBaller's top 50 RB group.

40.name: Blake Corum
40.comment: Corum got more chances last year and even split some work late in the year with starter Kyren Williams. He had double-digit carries four of his last five games and eight total for the season. Corum was 40th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had five games with double-digit fantasy points. Corum ran for 746 yards and averaged 5.1 yards per carry despite not starting a single game all season. He made a name for himself with his chances. Corum should play a similar role this year for the Rams, serving as the top backup to Williams. Corum is a good between the tackles runner that can churn out the yards. He also is very good in short-yardage situations. Corum is a solid pass catcher and willing blocker. He does lack some top-end speed and isn't the biggest back. And he is yet to have double-digit receptions in two seasons.
40.outlook: After a quiet 2024 rookie campaign, Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum emerged in his second season as first a usable flex play and then a bona fide week-winner. With the Rams' sights set on a deep postseason run, they seemed to make a concerted effort to keep primary back Kyren Williams as fresh as possible, and after Williams opened the season with 19 touches per game through the first nine weeks, that average fell below 16 from Weeks 10 through 18. With 2025 fourth-round pick Jarquez Hunter relegated to special teams, those extra opportunities went entirely to Corum, and in adding an element of explosiveness to the backfield, he finished the year with 746 yards on a team-leading 5.1 per carry. Corum was the fantasy RB17 over the final six weeks of the season, and his five rushing touchdowns in that span were topped only by Derrick Henry's seven. For the first time since 2016, the Rams did not add a running back through the NFL Draft, so his role appears secured heading into year three, and with Los Angeles again an early Super Bowl favorite, it would stand to reason that keeping Williams fresh would still be a priority. Even as a change of pace back, the former third-round pick out of Michigan will continue to offer standalone flex value, but should Williams miss extended time, something he has not done since 2023, Corum would greatly exceed his price tag of RotoBaller's RB35.

41.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
41.comment: Tracy topped 1,000 total yards for the second straight season. He had 1,028 total yards in 15 games, including 11 starts. Tracy was 28th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had just five games all year with double-digit fantasy points. He didn't produce great numbers despite getting to start over half the season. Cam Skattebo emerged as the starter for New York his rookie year before getting hurt. He will return to that No. 1 back role, moving Tracy down the depth chart. Tracy should still have a role offensively but won't get near the touches of his first two years. Tracy is a big-play threat with top moves in space. He catches the ball well and can be a solid three-down back. He can get to the next level in a hurry. Tracy is still learning how to setup his blocks and run better on the inside. He also doesn't make a ton of plays after contact at this stage of his career, averaging just 1.7 yards per carry after contact for his career.
41.outlook: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. should see more work early in the 2026 season as starting RB Cam Skattebo (ankle) recovers from the gruesome injury that prematurely ended his 2025 season. We've seen flashes from Tracy at times, but he's also made terrible mistakes that have cost his team dearly, like backbreaking drops and massive whiffs in pass protection. The Giants would prefer for Skattebo to be their workhorse, though, and when he returns to full health, that's likely what he will be. The second-year pro is an archetypal bruiser with added upside in his high-end elusiveness and contact balance. Tracy will return to a change-of-pace role, but the reality is that Skattebo is better to have on the field on any given play. Tracy also isn't a high-end goal-line back. There's a small glimmer of upside in his former status as a wide receiver in college, but Skattebo is far better with the ball in his hands. Tracy is a mid-tier handcuff that could be worth starting in deeper fantasy leagues early in the season.

42.name: Aaron Jones
42.comment: Jones had some injury issues last year and showed some signs of decline. He did not top 90-rushing yards in a single game. Jones was 41st overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had 747 total yards and three touchdowns in 12 games. He averaged a career-worst 4.2 yards per carry. His rushing totals were his worst since his rookie season. Jones is 31 years old and age is becoming a real concern. The days of him being a full-time starter might be about over. He remains with the Vikings for this season but could lose out on more work to Jordan Mason. Jones is not the biggest back but has good speed and moves. He catches the ball well and is a big-play threat at the position. He is a much improved runner between the tackles and is a solid three-down back. Injuries can be an issue for Jones and his lack of plays after contact could continue to be an issue going forward at this point of his career.
42.outlook: Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. had an underwhelming second year in Minny, tallying 132 carries for 548 yards and two touchdowns on the ground over 12 games, with a hamstring injury forcing him to the injured reserve in September. He would add 28 catches for 199 yards and an additional TD, but overall, was only a top-20 weekly half-PPR RB four times, and never higher than 12th. Jordan Mason would punch in six rush TDs, average 4.8 yards per carry to Jones' 4.2 mark, more than double the missed tackles forced rate, and register a 56% success rate to Jones' 50% clip. Those in PPR formats can still lean on Jones as the clear receiving back. New signal-caller Kyler Murray completed 87% of his throws under nine yards last year, while JJ McCarthy mustered a 74% clip. And it is easy to chalk Jones' lesser rushing form up to the early IR stint, making him an intriguing rebound play in an improved offensive environment. For now, he still represents a good value with an early ADP of 124 as the RB40, considering his top-100 RotoBaller rank.

43.name: Jonathon Brooks
43.comment: Brooks has played three games in two NFL seasons. He missed all of last year, recovering from a torn ACL suffered his rookie season. He has a long injury history, so it isn't certain about his future in the NFL. He has suffered multiple ACL tears. If healthy, Brooks will compete for a role in the Panthers backfield. And if he can show his pre-injury explosiveness, his role could be big. When healthy, Brooks is the complete package at running back, doing well on three downs. He has good vision and hits the hole in a hurry. He also runs with some power and can do well after contact. Brooks is a willing blocker in pass protection and is a plus pass catcher.
43.outlook: Jonathon Brooks has emerged as a viable option to target at his current ADP, as he appears primed to make a long-awaited impact in Carolina's backfield rotation. Brooks became the first running back to be selected during the 2024 NFL Draft when the Panthers secured him in Round 2 (46th overall). Brooks' most prolific numbers at the collegiate level were assembled during his final season at Texas (2023), when he accumulated 1,139 rushing yards (103.5 per game), generated 10 rushing touchdowns, and captured 25 of his 30 targets. His contributions to Carolina's offense have been minimal (23 offensive snaps/12 touches/45 total yards) as a result of two ACL tears that he has sustained since November 2023. It remains unclear whether Brooks can fully recapture the degree of agility, elusiveness, and acceleration that he displayed before his injuries. However, Brooks is still just 22 years old despite the protracted delay in his involvement, and his performance during OTAs has been encouraging. Brooks should ultimately operate as Carolina's RB2 behind Chuba Hubbard, who will turn 27 on June 11. Hubbard averaged 8.9 attempts per game last season while failing to generate a run that exceeded 14 yards, and finishing just 44th in rush yards over expected (-39) per Next Gen Stats. Brooks could secure a respectable role while functioning in a rotation with Hubbard. Brooks' projected placement on the Panthers' depth chart also positions him to emerge as an effective handcuff, as he should seize a significant workload if Hubbard is forced to the sideline. That makes Brooks an enticing option at his Round 9 ADPs in dynasty startups (98/RB32) and best ball leagues (107/RB37).

44.name: Alvin Kamara
44.comment: A knee injury cut short Kamara's season but he was having a down year before getting hurt in Week 12. He had five games with double-digit fantasy points but didn't reach 20 points in any game. He averaged a career-worst 3.6 yards per carry and 59.7 total yards per game. Kamara was 53rd in running back scoring, finishing outside the top 20 for just the second time in his career. Until last year, Kamara had at least 1,100 total yards every season in the NFL. Kamara will turn 31 years old before the start of the season. His days of being the top standalone back for a team seem about over. He is likely to be in more of a platoon role at this stage of his career, especially after showing signs of slowing down last year. Kamara is a playmaker. He can line up as a receiver as well as a running back. He has plus hands and can get to the next level in a hurry. Kamara also runs with power despite not being the biggest back.
44.outlook: Kamara is not near the back of past years. He could rebound a little this year. His receiving ability gives him fantasy value but don't expect him to be that top fantasy back of past years. He is going to be more of a flex play or spot starer. Kamara can get around 1,100 total yards, 50 receptions and five or six touchdowns.

45.name: Kenneth Gainwell
45.comment: Gainwell had his best season as a pro, forming a great rapport with quarterback Aaron Rodgers. He had 1,023 total yards and finished 16th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had four games with 20-plus fantasy points. He had seven games total with 16-plus fantasy points. Gainwell was most effective as a receiver, catching 73 passes for 486 yards. He also averaged a career-high 4.7 yards per carry and 2.1 yards per carry after contact. Gainwell averaged 2.1 yards per carry after contact, showing great power despite not being the biggest back. Gainwell might have a hard time getting the work he did last season but should be a solid third-down back for his new team, the Bucs. Gainwell catches the ball extremely well and can even line up in the slot. His lack of size is a bit of a concern for him to be a three-down back but he showed well in that role last year. Gainwell does his best work on the outside in space and in the passing game. He is an improving inside runner but still doesn't excel in that area.
45.outlook: Kenneth Gainwell assembled the most prolific numbers of his career during 2025 and is now primed to seize a sizable role in Tampa Bay's reconstructed backfield. Gainwell easily exceeded expectations while delivering career-best numbers in attempts (114/6.7 per game), rushing yards (537/31.6 per game), targets (85/5.0 per game), and receiving yards (486/28.6 per game), securing a career high 50% snap share and finishing as an RB1 during seven matchups. Gainwell also finished second among all backs in targets (51/6.4 per game), receptions (44/5.5 per game), and receiving yards (262/45.4 per game) from Weeks 11-18, and led his position in yards per route run (1.95). Gainwell's performance also propelled him to a two-year, $14 million contract with Tampa Bay. This will infuse Gainwell into a depth chart that also contains Bucky Irving, who will operate as the Buccaneers' lead back. However, Gainwell's presence should prevent Irving from functioning as a workhorse. Irving was sidelined during seven contests last season (foot/shoulder), and his averages in yards per attempt (3.4) and yards after contact per attempt (1.6) were uninspiring. Gainwell's versatility should propel him to a weekly allotment of carries while maintaining a role as Tampa Bay's primary receiving weapon from the backfield. Gainwell's proven ability to capitalize on those opportunities should sustain his standalone value. Gainwell also remains capable of approaching RB1 production if Irving is forced to the sideline. That justifies targeting Gainwell at his Round 9 ADP in best ball leagues (108/RB37), along with his Round 11 ADP in dynasty startups (121/RB41).

46.name: Isiah Pacheco
46.comment: Pacheco had another disappointing season despite starting much of the year. He had 563 total yards and two touchdowns in 13 games. Pacheco had just three games all season with double-digit fantasy points. He did not top 60-rushing yard in a single game and averaged just 3.9 yards per carry. Pacheco is trending the wrong way since his first two years in the NFL. He has averaged fewer than four yards per carry each of his last two seasons. A change of scenery is likely a good thing for Pacheco, heading to the Lions. He should be the top backup for Detroit, playing in an offense that does like to rotate their backs. Pacheco is a good inside runner that does well in bouncing off tacklers and making plays after contact. He also catches the ball pretty well. He runs very violently despite lacking some size. He will try to make the big play a little too often, limiting his yards.
46.outlook: Running back Isiah Pacheco began his career as an explosive, efficient option for the Chiefs, but his effectiveness has been limited since he fractured his fibula early in the 2024 season. Pacheco totaled only 563 yards and two touchdowns in 13 games in 2025. Worse, he has now finished with under 4.0 yards per carry two years in a row, and he has just two breakaway runs over the past two years compared to 19 in his first two. Now, Pacheco has joined the Detroit Lions on a one-year deal, replacing the departing David Montgomery. He will operate behind star tailback Jahmyr Gibbs, although the extent of his likely workload is uncertain. While Montgomery found plenty of success in a complementary role with Gibbs, Pacheco represents a downgrade at this point. However, the Lions have a great offense for fantasy purposes, a fact that should not change even with the introduction of new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. Pacheco should also be used more in the red zone with Detroit, leading to more scoring opportunities. He has been going as the RB50 in fantasy drafts, and despite his recent struggles, Pacheco provides value at that price.

47.name: Tyler Allgeier
47.comment: Allgeier was the top backup to Bijan Robinson once again last year and served that role very well. He ended up getting a lot of the goal-line work and had a career-best eight touchdowns. Allgeier was 39th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had five games with double-digit fantasy points. His yardage numbers were down a little, though, having 514-rushing yards, which was the lowest total of his four-year career. Allgeier serves the top backup role really well and should have that role once again this year, playing behind rookie Jeremiyah Love. Allgeier has starting experience and some success in that role. Allgeier is a former 1,000-yard rusher that averages 4.3 yards per carry. Allgeier is good at reading the play and producing with his chances. He churns out the yards and can make some big plays along the way. He is just a so-so pass catcher, having 61 receptions in four seasons.
47.outlook: Former Falcons running back Tyler Allgeier had a so-so 2025 season in his fourth year with the team. Allgeier's rushing yards fell to just 514 despite playing all 17 games. Moreover, his efficiency dropped, as he averaged just 3.5 true yards per carry, down from 4.6. He still finished as the RB45 on a per-game basis, though, due to his eight touchdowns. Allgeier now joins the Arizona Cardinals after signing a two-year deal worth $12.25 million. Though the solid payday suggested he'd start for the squad over James Conner and Trey Benson, the Arizona backfield transformed when the Cardinals drafted former Notre Dame star Jeremiyah Love with the third pick in April. Love was drafted to be the team's top tailback, but Allgeier is clearly part of Arizona's plans as well. Allgeier had nine games with double-digit carries a year ago behind Bijan Robinson, and he could see a similar workload situationally this year as a powerful back. With Allgeier going as the RB44 in drafts, though, is that a chance worth taking at his current price? Given his decline in efficiency and the promise of his new teammate, the answer right now is "no."

48.name: Zach Charbonnet
48.comment: Charbonnet was 25th in fantasy running back scoring for the second straight season. He did well as the top backup for the Seahawks, splitting a lot of the work with Kenneth Walker. Charbonnet had nine games with double-digit fantasy points. He had a career-high 730-rushing yards and 12 touchdowns. He got a lot of the goal-line work and excelled in that area for Seattle. Unfortunately, Charbonnet tore his ACL in the playoffs and now has a long road back. He is likely to miss the early part of the season as he recovers. Charbonnet has 870-plus total yards and at least nine touchdowns two straight seasons. Charbonnet is a good at hitting the hole in the hurry and churning out the yards. He also catches the ball well, serving as a legit three-down back. Charbonnet has 95 receptions in three seasons. He isn't the best outside runner, though, and can lack a little top-end speed.
48.outlook: One of the Seattle Seahawks' most productive skill players in 2025 was running back Zach Charbonnet (knee), but a January ACL tear in the team's NFC Divisional-Round game against the 49ers has created doubt about Charbonnet's early-season availability for 2026. He underwent surgery on February 20 to repair his left knee. According to NFL.com's Kevin Patra, head coach Mike McDonald hasn't ruled out Charbonnet being available for Week 1, but it seems like an unlikely timeline - roughly nine months from the injury. Seattle's championship-winning duo has been split up by both Charbonnet's injury and Kenneth Walker III's departure in free agency, so the team has reshaped its backfield with first-round rookie Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson joining George Holani (24 touches in 2025) in what seems to be an open, three-way competition. Considering that's an entirely unproven group, it is possible that Charbonnet, who totaled 874 scrimmage yards and 12 touchdowns in a reserve role behind Walker III, is the lead tailback when he's healthy and at full speed. Still, that's a challenging timeline to project at this stage. His situation has also slightly changed, given that last year's offensive playcaller, Klint Kubiak, has departed for the head coaching job in Las Vegas. RotoBaller's overall PPR rankings slot Charbonnet at No. 204 overall due to the uncertainty, but he might be a worthwhile late-round dart if a more positive prognosis is provided closer to the preseason. In dynasty formats, it's likely optimal to hold Charbonnet to see if he can finally take advantage of a backfield without Walker III and assume the lead role.

49.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
49.comment: Robinson was the top backup for the 49ers last year, playing behind Christian McCaffrey. Robinson did not have double-digit carries in a single game, but did have two games with double-digit fantasy points. He served the backup role well but didn't get much work with McCaffrey staying healthy all season. Robinson had 425 total yards and two touchdowns. He signed with the Falcons this offseason and will become the top backup to Bijan Robinson. Robinson averages just 4.1 yards per carry for his career and has never topped 800-rushing yards in a season. Robinson is a big back that does his best work between the tackles. He excels in short yardage and is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands. He isn't the most elusive back and doesn't always read the holes well. He is an improved pass catcher since entering the league but doesn't make a ton of plays in that area.
49.outlook: Atlanta Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr. steps into the role vacated by Tyler Allgeier after amassing 400 yards and two rushing touchdowns on 92 carries for the 49ers. He ran well behind workhorse Christian McCaffrey, who played in all 17 games, so we never saw BRob get featured throughout the 2025 campaign. Still, he ran well when given the chance, and wound up breaking as many tackles as he did in '24 on half of the number of rushes. This helped him achieve a 2.46 yards-after-contact-per-attempt rate, which ranked 10th among 51 RBs with 90 or more carries. The Falcons split rushing work between Bijan Robinson and Allgeier at nearly a perfect 2:1 ratio, with Allgeier seeing 143 carries and 16 targets. If Robinson falls into the same pattern of 7-10 carries per game, he could be viable as a flex play depending on how frequently the 2026 Falcons get into the red zone (Allgeier was the RB38 last year). And he's a top handcuff in case Bijan Robinson were unavailable, of course. While not a premier receiver like Bijan or CMC, he has caught 79% of career targets thrown his way, delivering a 36-368-4 air line in '23 for Washington. Our RotoBaller rank of RB47 likes him about 15 picks ahead of his late-June half-PPR ADP near the 162nd selection.

50.name: Justice Hill
50.comment: Hill was limited to 10 games last year because of a neck injury he suffered later in the year. He did well as the pass-catching back for the Ravens before getting hurt. He had 21 receptions for 169 yards in 10 games. He ran 19 times for 93 yards and two scores. Hill was 60th in running back scoring. He had one huge game in Week 4, which padded his numbers. He did little outside that game. Hill is a solid backup, doing well as a change-of-pace back. He will look to earn that role once again this season. He has 590-plus total yards two of three seasons. Hill is a speed back. He can make a lot of plays on the outside and get down the field in a hurry. Hill is not much of an inside runner, though, and tends to try to make the big play too often.
50.outlook: Hill is not a bad No. 4 or 5 fantasy back. He isn't going to post huge numbers but has a decent floor because of his work in the passing game. He will get some weekly work. Hill can get around 500 total yards and a few scores.

51.name: Ty Johnson
51.comment: Johnson has posted similar numbers the last two seasons as a reserve back for the Bills. He had 463 total yards and five touchdowns last year. He was 47th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had three games with double-digit fantasy points. Johnson has 350-plus total yards five of seven seasons. Johnson can serve the change-of-pace role well and will look to grab that job again this season. He has top speed. Johnson can get to the next level in a hurry and does well in space. He lacks a little power, though, and does not do that great after contact. He catches the ball pretty well and can be an asset in the passing game.
51.outlook: Johnson might get some total yards but is not likely to make much of a fantasy impact. If he has a big game, you just never know when that might happen. He could get around 400 total yards and 25 receptions.

52.name: Keaton Mitchell
52.comment: Mitchell emerged as the top backup to Derrick Henry last season and performed very well in that role. He averaged an impressive 5.8 yards per carry, showing great explosiveness. He had 404 total yards in 13 games. Mitchell signed with the Chargers this offseason and will compete with Kimani Vidal for the top backup job. Mitchell would seem a great fit for the Chargers new offense, using his top speed in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' scheme. Mitchell lacks a little size, but has great speed and moves in space. He makes plays with the ball in his hands. His lack of size is a bit of a concern for his durability going forward, especially if you consider the time he has missed each of his first three seasons. He has suffered some major injuries to start his career.
52.outlook: Los Angeles Chargers running back Keaton Mitchell has never lacked explosiveness. The former Ravens back has averaged an eye-popping 6.8 yards per touch across his first three NFL seasons, but at only 5'8" and 191 pounds, a concerning injury history has limited him to just 144 total opportunities during that span. Now in Los Angeles on a two-year deal, Mitchell lands with an offensive coordinator in Mike McDaniel who has long prioritized speed as a defining trait in his backfields, previously turning largely unproven veteran Raheem Mostert into a Pro Bowler and the RB2 in 2023 before helping to make De'Von Achane one of the most valuable players in fantasy. Mitchell is expected to operate primarily as a change-of-pace option behind 2025 first-round pick Omarion Hampton, but even on modest volume, the 2023 undrafted free agent has consistently demonstrated an ability to generate chunk plays, and a larger complementary role could easily lead to the most productive season of his career. Mitchell is now two and a half years removed from the ACL tear that cut short his rookie season and lingered into his second campaign, and at just 24 years old, he enters 2026 with both youth and elite athleticism on his side. While his weekly workload may prove difficult to project outside of best ball formats, Mitchell offers enough upside to make him a late-round target or priority waiver add in deeper leagues, and at RotoBaller's RB39, he could offer enough standalone flex value to keep him rostered throughout the season, even without needing an injury ahead of him.

53.name: Jonah Coleman
53.comment: Denver added another back to their running back room, taking Coleman in the fourth round of this year's draft. Coleman is a solid three-down back. He catches the ball well and is a willing blocker. He is a smaller back but is well built and pretty good after contact because of his size. He lacks a little top-end speed. Coleman will battle for a depth role at running back his rookie season. He could carve out a solid role with a strong camp and preseason.
53.outlook: Denver Broncos' rookie running back Jonah Coleman joins the team as a fourth-round draft selection. The 22-year-old had a productive college career at Arizona and Washington as a do-it-all back, and now joins a stacked backfield with J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey. It remains to be seen what type of role Coleman can carve out in this offense, as he is a good pass-catcher, pass-blocker, and goal line back. He caught 87 passes in his college career, and scored 34 rushing touchdowns. Dobbins profiles as the early-down back in this offense, while Harvey is more of a change-of-pace type of back. It may take a few weeks for Coleman to get mixed into the lineup, but one injury to Dobbins or Harvey could give him the opportunity needed to make an impact as a rookie.

54.name: Devin Singletary
54.comment: Singletary served a backup role for the Giants for a second straight season and finished with the exact same rushing yards (437). Singletary was third on the depth chart earlier in the year when Cam Skattebo was healthy. He saw his playing time increase once Skattebo was injured, though. Singletary played his best later in the season, having double-digit fantasy points five of his last eight games. Singletary had three straight seasons with 1,000-plus total yards before his last two seasons with the Giants. He can make plays in an expanded role but probably is best suited as a top backup, a role he likely serves this year. Singletary is a speed back, getting to the next level in a hurry. He can make plays as a runner and receiver, making him a three-down threat. Singletary is not a great runner on the inside, though, but has improved in that area since earlier in his career.
54.outlook: Singletary is likely to play a similar backup role at this stage of his career. This won't help a lot of of fantasy teams. He could get around 500 total yards and a few scores.

55.name: Tank Bigsby
55.comment: Bigsby fell down the depth chart in Jacksonville and was traded to the Eagles early last season. He was the top backup for Philadelphia much of the year and had 376 total yards and two touchdowns in 16 games for the Eagles. He had a 100-yard rushing game in Week 8. He had two games with double-digit fantasy points. Bigsby should get first shot to be the top backup for the Eagles this season. Bigsby is more of a power back that does his best work between the tackles. He has averaged at least 2.7 yards per carry after contact each of the last two seasons. He also has good moves in space for man of his size. His not much of a pass catcher, though, and will be little help in the passing game.
55.outlook: Philadelphia Eagles running back Tank Bigsby ran with purpose when given a chance in 2025, averaging 5.9 yards per carry on 58 totes following an early in-season trade to Philly. The initial motivation for the deal followed Will Shipley's Week 1 oblique/rib injury, as the Eagles needed RB depth and a kickoff returner. The 5-foot-11 runner didn't log a rush until Week 7, when his one touch went for 11 yards. In Week 8, he gashed the Giants for 104 yards on just nine carries. With Saquon Barkley resting in Week 18, Bigsby notched 106 total yards and a score on 17 touches. While he was a lightning rod with the ball, he rarely saw work when the game was close. With regression expected across the ball for the Eagles offense, as well as a lighter strength of schedule for 2026, that condition should be eased. Given the solid offensive line and scoring environment, and with an offseason to potentially work him into the game plan, Bigsby is at least an elite handcuff as the RB55 near his early half-PPR 172 ADP.

56.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
56.comment: Rodriguez got the most work of his career, getting a chance to start seven games because of injury. He had 530 total yards and six touchdowns, helping him finish 52nd overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had four games with double-digit fantasy points. He averaged a solid 4.5 yards per carry. Rodriguez also made a ton of plays after contact, tying for the league lead in yards per carry after contact (3.0). Rodriguez will look to earn the top backup job for his new team, the Jaguars. Rodriguez is a power back that finishes his runs well and can get downhill in a hurry. He lacks a little burst and does not have great moves in space. He also isn't much of a pass catcher, having six receptions in three seasons.
56.outlook: Rodriguez might have a hard time getting as much work this year as he did last season but still has some late-round value. He could find the end zone a few times and will get some weekly touches in what should be a good offense once again. He might get 600 total yards and a few scores.

57.name: Dylan Sampson
57.comment: Sampson played backup role his rookie year and even got a couple starts because of injury. He had 446 total yards and two touchdowns. Sampson did most of his damage as a pass catcher, catching 33 passes for 271 yards. He served the third-down role well. Sampson will look to earn that role this coming year for the Browns. Sampson is an explosive player that does well in space. Sampson is a solid pass catcher and change-of-pace back. He got a few starts last year but showed he likely isn't an every-down back just yet in the NFL. He can struggle to make plays on the inside.
57.outlook: Many were disappointed by Dylan Sampson's landing spot with the Cleveland Browns in the 2025 NFL Draft, considering the same team selected another rookie, Quinshon Judkins (ankle), with a top-40 pick. Judkins' summer legal issues opened the door for Sampson to earn major snaps early last season. Still, he failed to truly separate from a committee that included Jerome Ford and Raheim Sanders. He ultimately earned just 32 carries from Judkins' season debut in Week 2 to Week 16, where the starter suffered a dislocated ankle against the Bills. Sampson saw double-digit carries in both weeks that Judkins missed to end the season, but they resulted in more of the same efficiency issues that plagued him all year behind a miserable Browns offensive line. While the former Volunteers star managed a poor 2.7 yards per carry on the ground, he managed 8.2 yards per reception across 32 catches (on 40 targets). That was a bit of a stunner when receiving was seen as a hole in his prospect profile after just 37 catches total in his final two seasons at Tennessee. With Ford departing for the Washington Commanders in free agency, Sampson now has a clear path to receiving work behind Judkins for 2026, and he's a premium handcuff should the star second-year back suffer another injury. Though uncertainty remains in Cleveland's quarterback situation as Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson battle it out during training camp. The arrow is undoubtedly pointed upward for the Browns' offense under new coach Todd Monken after massive overhauls to the offensive line and wide receiver rooms during free agency and April's draft. Cleveland drafted wide receivers Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, and OT Spencer Fano with their first three picks. Sampson isn't a priority in standard leagues. Still, catching passes will provide some weekly value in PPR formats, where he is ranked 178th overall at RotoBaller with a Sleeper ADP of 165. He's a candidate to be one of those late-round fliers at running back who becomes a weekly starter should an injury occur above him on the depth chart. It's worth noting that Judkins is progressing well in his recovery from an ankle injury, making Sampson mainly a handcuff for Judkins managers or an option in PPR or best ball formats.

58.name: Sean Tucker
58.comment: Tucker was third on the Bucs depth chart most of the year. He got expanded chances a few games, rushing 19 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns in Week 11. He had three games with double-digit rush attempts. Tucker had 354 total yards and eight touchdowns. He was 50th overall in fantasy running back scoring. His value was lifted because of his touchdown totals, getting a chance to get some short-yardage work. Tucker will look to play a bigger role this year and serve as a top backup. Tucker is a big-play back that can get to the next level in a hurry. He is elusive in the open field. Tucker also runs with a little power and can make plays after contact.
58.outlook: The NFL journey of Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Sean Tucker was complicated by medical concerns that led to him going undrafted in the 2023 NFL Draft, but he has risen to the occasion whenever given opportunities. Tucker emerged as a valuable complementary piece in Tampa Bay's backfield in 2025, leading the team with seven rushing touchdowns and carving out a significant role near the goal line. With Bucky Irving still working his way back from the shoulder injury that sidelined him for seven games last season and appeared to limit his effectiveness upon his return, Tucker's usage could carry over into 2026. Over the second half of the season, Tucker handled the overwhelming majority of the Buccaneers' carries inside the five-yard line, racking up seven of his eight total touchdowns after Week 7 and establishing himself as the team's preferred short-yardage option. While Irving remains the favorite to lead the backfield in overall touches, Tampa Bay may choose to manage his workload after last year's injury issues. If so, Tucker stands to benefit more than veteran addition Kenneth Gainwell, who profiles more as a direct replacement to pass-catching back Rachaad White. In an offense expected to generate scoring chances once again, Tucker has the touchdown upside to greatly outperform his current ranking of RotoBaller's RB65, and as a player going largely undrafted, he could provide weekly flex value if his red zone role remains intact.

60.name: Mike Washington Jr.
60.comment: Washington didn't land in a great spot for playing time. He was drafted by the Raiders in the fourth round of this years's draft. He will be behind star back Ashton Jeanty. Washington has good burst and hits the hole in a hurry. He isn't the biggest back and doesn't do great after contact. Washington is not good in pass protection, which could impact his playing time early in his career. He has a good chance to be the top backup his rookie season.
60.outlook: Talent-wise, Las Vegas Raiders rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. is one of the most talented backs from the 2026 draft class. Washington posted a perfect Relative Athletic Score after the 223-pound back ran a 4.33 40-time and sported a 39" vertical. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak hinted all along that they wanted a second running back in Las Vegas to push Ashton Jeanty and to help alleviate some of the workload. Considering the Raiders had one of the worst offensive lines last season, they decided to add another option in the backfield. How bad were the Raiders' offensive line woes? Jeanty had 975 rushing yards after contact, which would end up being 65% of his total rushing yardage during his rookie season. While all the coach talk suggests that Washington has standalone value as a possible flex option for fantasy managers, Washington will not be a league winner unless Jeanty misses significant time. While Washington did churn out 1,070 rushing yards at Arkansas last season, he also caught 28 passes for 226 receiving yards, which shouldn't be lost here. Last season, when Kirk Cousins was under center, Cousins 11.2% check down rate was the fifth-highest. Considering the state of the Raiders' wide receiver room, checking down the ball to Washington as a change of pace option could make the Raiders' fifth-worst passing attack from a season ago look better on paper. Washington is expected to be the Raiders' No. 2 back behind Jeanty. The 22-year-old is currently ranked 201st overall at RotoBaller, which aligns with his Sleeper ADP of 191 in redraft leagues for upcoming fantasy football drafts.

61.name: Alexander Mattison
61.comment: Mattison missed all of last year because of a neck injury suffered before the season. He needed surgery on the injury. He had 700-plus total yards each of his previous two seasons before this injury. Mattison will look to earn a top backup job this year, a role he can serve well. He is just 27 years old, so he has plenty left in the tank. Mattison has 400-plus rushing yards five of the six seasons he has played in the NFL. Mattison is a big, powerful back that does best between the tackles. He lacks a little top-end speed and won't make a ton of plays to the outside. But he is a power back that can make plays after contact and move the pile. He also is a much improved pass catcher that can be an asset in the passing game.
61.outlook: Mattison might get a few weekly touches in a reserve role but carries little fantasy value. He might get 500 total yards and a few scores.

62.name: Jerome Ford
62.comment: Ford fell way down the depth chart in Cleveland last year, moving behind the two rookie backs. Ford had 176 total yards after two straight seasons with 780-plus total yards. Ford had just a game all year with double-digit fantasy points, which came in Week 2. Ford signed with the Commanders and will look to earn a backup role with his new team. Ford is a big, physical back with good speed. He lacks some moves in space, though, and doesn't have great vision. He is a more than capable pass catcher that can serve as a three-down back in the NFL.
62.outlook: Ford could see an uptick in playing time this year with the Commanders but still will be hit or miss in a backup role. He is not worth a roster spot unless injury hits. He can get around 400 total yards and a few scores.

63.name: Antonio Gibson
63.comment: Gibson had a season-ending ACL tear in Week 5. He had 112 total yards in a reserve role before getting hurt. Gibson serves the backup role well and will look to earn that role again this year. He has a long road back from his ACL tear and might not be ready for the start of the year. Gibson has 1,000-plus total yards two of six seasons. At this point, he seems stuck in more of a pass-catching role going forward. His days of being an every-down back as he was early in his career might be about over. Gibson has elite speed and is a top receiver out of the backfield. He can get to the next level in a hurry and catches the ball well. Gibson also can do pretty well between the tackles when given the chance. He can get it done inside and outside.
63.outlook: Gibson has some value as a reserve back if he is healthy. He will get some consistent yards and receptions on a weekly basis in a reserve role. Just don't expect big numbers. He might get around 500 total yards and a score or two.

64.name: Braelon Allen
64.comment: There was hope for Allen to play a bigger role in the Jets offense last year, but that didn't come to fruition. He had 18 carries for 76 yards and a touchdown in four games before hurting his knee. He suffered a knee sprain and was unable to return the rest of the season. But even when playing, he got limited work as the Jets top backup. He is expected to play a similar role this year. Allen is a bruising back that does his best work on the inside. He runs with power and is a load to bring down with the ball in his hands. He lacks some wiggle, though, and his speed is just so so for the position. He also catches the ball pretty well for a man of his size.
64.outlook: Braelon Allen is primed to operate as the Jets' RB2, which is the role that Allen secured before he sustained a season-ending MCL sprain last September. Allen was averaging 4.5 attempts/19.0 rushing yards per game before his injury, and had accumulated a team-high six attempts inside the red zone during that span. Allen also captured a higher snap share than Isaiah Davis (24%/19.8%) during those matchups, which underscored his status as the preferred backup to Hall. Allen has fully recovered and is positioned to re-emerge directly below Hall on New York's depth chart. That will also cement Allen as an insurance policy for Hall, whose unquestioned status as the Jets' lead back was confirmed when he signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract in May. Hall's presence should impede Allen from seizing a sizable workload. However, the 22-year-old Allen possesses a favorable blend of size, vision, and power. That facilitates his ability to secure opportunities in short-yardage and goal-line situations. Allen would also emerge as New York's temporary lead rusher if Hall is sidelined for any reason. This makes Allen a viable handcuff option, even though Davis would siphon a percentage of targets during any absence by Hall. It also supplies the rationale for selecting Allen at his Round 14 ADP in dynasty startups (167/RB56), along with his Round 18 ADP in best ball leagues (210/RB60).

65.name: Kareem Hunt
65.comment: Hunt ended up being the top back for the Chiefs many weeks and finished 31st overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had six games with double-digit fantasy points, including a game with 21 points in Week 12. Hunt had 754 total yards and nine touchdowns on the season. He has more than 1,600 total yards his last two seasons with the Chiefs, having a big resurgence after some down years. He is 31 years old, though, and likely going to serve a reserve role this season. Hunt is a former 1,000-yard rusher. He is a big back that hits the hole in a hurry and does a good job of reading his blocks. He is a dependable three-down back. He catches the ball well and has decent moves in space.
65.outlook: Hunt rebounded in a big way the last two years after a few down seasons but is going to have a hard time matching those numbers unless injury hits. He might be worth a look in deeper formats but that is about it. He could get around 500 total yards and four or five touchdowns.

66.name: Jaylen Wright
66.comment: Wright was buried on the depth chart early last year but got some chances the second half of the season and played pretty well with his chances. He had a 100-yard rushing game Week 14. He had 332 total yards in 10 games. Wright averaged 4.1 yards per carry. He has a lot to compete with for carries in Miami, though, and likely is third or fourth on the depth chart once again this year. Wright can be electric with the ball in his hands. He does well as a receiver and can make big plays after the catch. He isn't too polished as an inside runner, though, and lacks a little thump at the position.
66.outlook: Wright is going to be boom or bust on a weekly basis. He will have some big games along the way but likely disappear in others. Wright is worth a late-round look for fantasy teams. He can get around 500 total yards, 20 receptions and a few scores.

67.name: Emanuel Wilson
67.comment: Wilson was the top backup for the Packers for a second straight season and finished with very similar numbers to the past season. He had 595 total yards and three touchdowns. Wilson was 48th overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had four games with double-digit fantasy points. Wilson made some plays with his chances. He will look to earn some carries with the Seahawks this year, trying to win their No. 2 or 3 job. Wilson can serve as a three-down back, doing a little bit of everything pretty well. He is more of a power back, breaking nine tackles in limited rush attempts last year. He does lack a little wiggle, though, and doesn't have elite speed for the position.
67.outlook: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson comes over from Green Bay at an opportune time to establish himself as a trustworthy rusher early in the year. Zach Charbonnet is recovering from a torn ACL suffered in the playoffs and should miss time in '26, which has first-round pick Jadarian Price and a third-year George Holani alongside Wilson on the depth chart. Price's draft capital and skills should get the inside track, but Wilson can't be written off. He grabbed headlines in Week 12 of last season when he turned 30 total touches into 125 yards and a pair of touchdowns when Josh Jacobs was out. Wilson has averaged 4.5 yards per carry in his career and posted a 4.1 YPC in the five games he saw double-digit carries in '25. Keep an eye on Price's involvement this preseason, as Wilson could find 12-15 touches per game in September. He's an easy late-round click near his half-PPR 186 ADP (RotoBaller rank: 168) for those stashing picks who need time to blossom.

68.name: Nicholas Singleton
68.comment: The Titans took Singleton in the fifth round of this year's draft. He lands in a good spot to possibly earn some playing time his rookie year. He doesn't have a lot of top options ahead of him on the depth chart. He is a good one-cut runner and big-play threat in the running game. Singleton runs a little upright for the pro game. Singleton also catches the ball pretty well and can be an asset in pass protection.
68.outlook: Singleton might be worth a late-round look for fantasy teams. He could end up earning some work in this offense. Look for around 500 total yards and a few scores.

69.name: Kaleb Johnson
69.comment: Johnson had a really disappointing rookie season. He was buried on the depth chart and failed to top 25-rushing yards in a single game. Johnson had 78 total yards in 10 games. He could move up the depth chart this year but will need a strong offseason and camp for that to happen. Johnson isn't the most explosive back but is good between the tackles and can carry the load. He will make plays after contact. He will drop some passes but catches the ball pretty well and is a willing blocker.
69.outlook: Johnson can't do much worse than last year. He could improve but don't expect a big enough jump to be a big fantasy factor. He will still struggle to get consistent work. Johnson might be worth a look in deeper formats as a late-round pick. Look for around 500 total yards, 10 receptions and a few touchdowns.

70.name: James Conner
70.comment: Conner played just three games before suffering a season-ending foot injury. He failed to top 40-rushing yards in an of his three games despite having double-digit carries two of those game. He had some struggles before getting hurt. Conner had two straight 1,000-yard seasons before last year. He is 31 years old and has a bit of an injury history. He is expected to be second or third on the depth chart for the Cardinals this year. Conner has never played a full season in nine years. Conner can be an explosive player. He does well between the tackles but also has enough speed to make plays on the outside. He also will run through defenders and make a lot of plays after contact. Conner is a solid pass catcher, showing three-down ability.
70.outlook: Conner is trending the wrong way and now has a generational talent ahead of him on the depth chart in Arizona. He might be worth a late-round pick but that is about it. Look for around 500 total yards, 10 receptions and a touchdown or two.

71.name: Samaje Perine
71.comment: Perine was back with the Bengals last year and played his usual top backup role. He played well as the top backup to Chase Brown, finishing with 469 total yards. He averaged a solid 4.5 yards per carry and scored three touchdowns. He did get two starts because of injury and had two games with double-digit fantasy points. Perine does well as a top backup, role he will compete for again this year. He is a solid pass catcher, having 27 or more receptions four of five seasons. Perine does well between the tackles and has a knack for finding the end zone. He doesn't have great moves in space, though, and doesn't break a lot of big plays to the outside. Perine is a much improved pass catcher as evident by his numbers the past few seasons.
71.outlook: Perine is worth a late-round pick for fantasy teams in deeper formats. He has a decent floor because of his work in the passing game. He won't post big weekly numbers but will at least put up some numbers each week. He should be able to get around 400 total yards, 20 receptions and a few scores.

72.name: Nick Chubb
72.comment: Chubb had his best seasons in a few years, getting a chance to start nine games for the Texans. He had 573 total yards and three touchdowns. He was 55th overall in fantasy running back scoring. Chubb had double-digit fantasy points two his first five games but didn't reach that mark again after Week 5. Chubb moved to more of a reserve role as the season progressed but served that role well. He averaged 2.1 yards per carry after contact. Chubb should serve a similar reserve role this coming season. He is a former 1,000-yard rusher but hasn't topped 525-rushing yards three straight seasons. Chubb is a very big back with good vision and the ability to run through tacklers. He doesn't have elite speed but enough to make plays on the outside. Chubb is a tough runner to bring down and does a good job of making plays after contact. He isn't a great pass catcher, though, limiting his fantasy ceiling.
72.outlook: Chubb had a little value last year but to much. Expect more of the same, making him a stretch for fantasy teams to draft. He might get around 500 total yards and a few scores.

73.name: Ray Davis
73.comment: It was thought that Davis might play a little bigger role in year two but that wasn't the case. His playing time actually decreased. He had 361 total yards and two touchdowns, And Davis did nearly all his damage the last week of the season, rushing 21 times for 151 yards in a game the Bills rested their starters much of the game. Davis might be stuck as the third-string back for the Bills once again this year, getting sporadic work in that role. Davis is a solid three-down back. He has good size for the position and can do well between the tackles. He also catches the ball well and does well after contact. Davis lacks a little vision, though, and can take a little while to get to the next level, lacking a little explosiveness.
73.outlook: Davis was 40th his rookie year and 60th last year in fantasy scoring. He has limited fantasy value right now. He might be worth a late-round gamble but that is about it. Look for around 400 total yards and a couple touchdowns with 15 receptions.

74.name: Kimani Vidal
74.comment: Vidal got 10 starts his second season, finding the field a lot more often because of some injuries at running back for the Chargers. He opened the season third or fourth on the depth chart. Vidal had 779 total yards and four touchdowns in 13 games. Vidal was 42nd overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had five games with double-digit fantasy points. He hit the 100-yard rushing mark three games. Vidal did average just 4.1 yards per carry and 1.8 yards per carry after contact. He got the volume but didn't make a ton of plays with his chances. Look for him to move down the depth chart this year and serve more of a No. 2 or 3 role for the Chargers, competing with Keaton Mitchell for the top backup job. Vidal is a powerful runner. He does well between the tackles and is tough to bring down once he gets going. Vidal also is a solid pass catcher, showing three-down ability. He isn't a speed back, though, and his moves in space are just alright.
74.outlook: Vidal might be worth a late-round speculative pick. He could get some weekly work if all goes well for him once again. He could get 400 total yards, 15 receptions and a few scores.

75.name: Jordan James
75.comment: James played just three games his rookie season, being inactive most weeks. James actually got his only work during the playoffs, rushing six times for 28 yards in the divisional round game. The 49ers apparently really like what they have in James, though, and will give him a chance to compete for the top backup job. James is an elusive runner that runs with power. He can make plays after contact. James also is a decent pass catcher and can help as a blocker in pass protection. He is just a so-so athlete for the position.
75.outlook: James will have obvious fantasy value if he wins the backup job. He is a player to watch this preseason and training camp.

76.name: Najee Harris
76.comment: Harris competed for the Chargers starting job last year but was unable to win the job. He played the first three games of the season before getting hurt. He had 15 carries for 61 yards before tearing his Achilles. He had four straight 1,000-yard seasons before last year. He will look to get it going again this year but nothing is certain, trying to return from this major injury. He could be slowed some early in the year. Harris averages just 3.9 yards per carry for his career, showing a lack of explosion. He gets the tough yards, though, and is a consistent back. Harris is a decent three-down back. He catches the ball well despite not getting a ton of work in that area throughout his career. He is best between the tackles. Harris has good moves in space and is a tough cover out of the backfield. He does lack a little elite speed, though, but is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands. He has broken 103 tackles in five seasons.
76.outlook: Harris has a lot of uncertainty surround him this year. He is a risk but worth a bench spot. Harris can get around 800 total yards, 20 receptions and four or five scores.

77.name: Isaiah Davis
77.comment: Davis ended up being the top backup for the Jets most of last year because of an injury to Braelon Allen early in the season. Davis had 422 total yards and a touchdown on the season, about doubling his production from his rookie year. Davis will compete for the top backup job this year but might have a hard time winning it after being pretty ho-hum with his chances last season. Davis is a big, productive back. He can churn out the yards. He does well after contact, using his size to his advantage. He is improving as a pass catcher but lacks a little burst.
77.outlook: Davis got the most work of his career last year but still didn't help fantasy teams. It is likely more of the same this year. He will struggle to get consistent touches.

78.name: Demond Claiborne
78.comment: The Vikings added another weapon to their backfield, taking Claiborne in the sixth round of this year's draft. He was a highly productive starter in college. He has great speed and does well into getting to the next level in a hurry. He is a good one-cut runner. He is good in the open field but also runs with some power despite lacking some size. Claiborne can do well as a three-down back. He also is a good return man and could help in that area immediately for the Vikings. For now, he is likely third on the depth chart at running back.
78.outlook: Claiborne is a little intriguing. He doesn't have great options ahead of him on the depth chart in Minnesota and could end up carving out a role in this offense. He might be worth a late-round dart throw.

79.name: MarShawn Lloyd
79.comment: Lloyd had another lost season because of various injuries. He didn't get in a game and has played a game in two seasons. Lloyd is running out of time to make an impression with the Packers. He is just hoping to keep a roster spot this season. Lloyd is a big, powerful back with plus speed. He runs with power and is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands. Lloyd is a solid pass catcher. He needs to work on his pass blocking, though, to get on the field often in that role.
79.outlook: Lloyd has done nothing in two seasons and plays behind a workhorse back. These are two pretty big strikes against him for this season. Lloyd probably isn't worth a draft pick but might be worth grabbing after the season starts and he has a role with the team.

80.name: Kaelon Black
80.comment: The 49ers picked Black in the third round of this year's draft, hoping to have found their new top backup at running back. Black is a very strong back that does his best work between the tackles. He has good vision and can get to the next level in a hurry. He plays through contact and has good balance. He got next to no work as a pass catcher in college, though, which is a concern as he transitions to the pro game. Black seems likely to be third on the depth chart his rookie year in San Francisco.
80.outlook: You never know with 49ers backs, so Black is worth a shot as a deep reserve for fantasy teams. If he wins the backup job, he will have obvious value as the handcuff to Christian McCaffrey.

81.name: Ollie Gordon II
81.comment: Gordon had just a game all year with double-digit carries. He was third on the depth chart much of his rookie season. He finished with 231 total yards and four touchdowns. His best attribute was his short-yardage work, finding the end zone four times. He served that role well. Gordon will look to earn the top backup job from day one this year, playing behind De'Von Achane. Gordon has the talented Jaylen Wright to compete with for the No. 2 job, though. Gordon is a big back that will move the pile and makes plays after contact. He can get downhill in a hurry. Gordon also is a decent pass catcher and can help in the passing game. He isn't a polished runner, though, didn't do much with his chances last year.
81.outlook: Gordon has some touchdown potential but that is about it. He will struggle to get consistent work. He might be worth a late-round look for fantasy teams.

82.name: Adam Randall
82.comment: The Ravens picked Randall in the fifth round of this year's draft. He is a converted receiver, making the switch to running back last year. He showed good promise at the new position. He runs with power and can get downhill quickly. Randall is a little upright right now and will need to work on his form at the next level. Randall also can be a big asset at receiver, being a former receiver. He could play a third-down role some his rookie season in Baltimore.
82.outlook: Few 2026 prospects had the meteoric rise that former Clemson running back Adam Randall did during the pre-draft process. As a converted wide receiver, Randall had just four career carries entering his final season with the Tigers, so his season - and pre-draft workouts - were graded on a curve for a developing player. Even with that, his "6-foot-2", 230-pound frame is elite for the position, and he had a nice year with 1,068 scrimmage yards amid a disastrous (6-6) season for Clemson's entire roster. Randall impressed at the Senior Bowl and the combine, where he posted a tremendous 4.50-second 40-yard dash for his size. He also, predictably, shined in receiving drills given his experience catching the ball. His NFL landing spot is extremely fascinating on multiple fronts. Randall joins an ambiguous Baltimore Ravens backfield that is totally up in the air behind Derrick Henry. Justice Hill has proven to be an effective scat back, but he may not be able to handle the load should something happen to Henry, and Rasheen Ali handled just seven carries last year. Obviously, the big bruiser comes with natural comparisons to Henry's frame, but there's an additional layer of intrigue, too. Ravens owner Steve Biscotti requested a Day 3 pick to use however he saw fit, and Biscotti used his personal connections to Dabo Swinney and the Clemson program to arrive on Randall as a high-character, high-potential selection. The inexperienced tailback will have to continue to develop his fluidity and vision as a runner at the pro level. Still, if any behind-the-scenes politics help him break free of Hill and Ali in an ambiguous race for the team's RB2 slot, Randall might play quite a bit in his rookie season should Henry battle an injury at any point.

83.name: Trey Benson
83.comment: Benson seemed setup for his shot to start after James Conner got hurt, but didn't last long, getting hurt himself. He suffered a knee injury and was unable to return before the season was over. Benson played four games, rushing 29 times for 160 yards. He averaged an impressive 5.5 yards per carry. Benson will compete with Tyler Allgeier and James Conner for touches behind rookie Jeremiyah Love this year in the Cardinals backfield. Benson has never topped 400 total yards in a season. Benson is a speed burner that can get to the next level in a hurry and is an asset in the passing game. He can get through the hole in a hurry but lacks a little patience at times.
83.outlook: Benson has too much to compete with for playing time right now in Arizona. He will have a hard time finding the field consistently unless injury hits.

84.name: Devin Neal
84.comment: Neal was starting to get some work late in the year but a hamstring injury ended his season a little early, missing the last three games. He had double-digit fantasy points three of his last four games played, though. Neal had 310 total yards in 10 games, including three starts. He made some plays with his chances. Neal should compete for the No. 2 or 3 job in New Orleans this year. Neal has good size and does well in setting up his blocks. He also can play all three downs. Neal lacks a little top speed, though, and his hands are a little small, which is a concern for fumbling and his work in the passing game.
84.outlook: Neal will be hit or miss in a reserve role. Expect his numbers to be similar to last year, getting 300 or 400 total yards.

85.name: Emmett Johnson
85.comment: Johnson was picked in the fifth round of this year's draft by the Chiefs. He should be the No. 3 or 4 back for the Chiefs his rookie season. Johnson does a good job of setting up his blocks and hitting the hole. He does not have great moves in space, though. Johnson rarely fumbled in college and showed well as a pass catcher. He has the talent to be a three-down back at the next level.
85.outlook: The Kansas City Chiefs selected running back Emmett Johnson in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. While not the fastest back, the 22-year-old has made a productive living thus far thanks to three quality traits. Those traits are elite vision, lateral agility, and pure efficiency. Running backs don't accidentally amass 1,451 rushing yards (5.8 per carry) and 370 receiving yards (46 receptions) in the Big Ten. Johnson is one of three backs in this year's draft class to force a missed tackle rate greater than 0.30 on 150-plus touches, which is impressive considering the strength of competition he had faced. More impressive yet, only 8.4% of Johnson's rushing attempts failed to gain positive yards. His rushing ability reminds some of Bucky Irving. At the same time, his receiving profile resembles Kenneth Walker III, who caught 87% of his intended targets and averaged 1.14 yards per route run over his collegiate career. Walker is hoping that Johnson doesn't factor into his touches in Kansas City's backfield the way Zach Charbonnet did in Seattle. If Walker were to miss time, the fifth-round rookie has everything the Chiefs need to keep the offense running at a high level. However, Johnson is competing with Brashard Smith and Emari Demercado for the backup role to Walker, making him at best a late-round flyer and dynasty stash heading into fantasy football draft season.

86.name: Ty Chandler
86.comment: Chandler was hurt Week 1 last year and didn't play again until Week 17. He played three games, rushing 17 times for 47 yards. Chandler signed with the Saints and will look to earn a reserve role with his new team. He serves the role well. Chandler has the makeup of a three-down back. He reads his blocks well and can be an effective pass catcher. Chandler does lack a little thump, though, and struggles at times hitting the hole in a hurry.
86.outlook: Chandler is more of a help on special teams than as a running back. He could see a slight uptick in playing time but not much. He might get 300 total yards with a score or two.

87.name: Austin Ekeler
87.comment: Ekeler suffered an Achilles' injury in Week 2 and was done for the season. He had 81 total yards in two games before the injury. Ekeler has a really long road back from this major injury at this stage of his career. He is expected to try to return, though, and should play a reserve role. Ekeler probably isn't a starter anymore, but can do well as a third-down back. Ekeler has never had a 1,000-yard rushing season during his career but has 50-plus catches five of his last seven seasons. Ekeler remains one of the better receiving backs in the game when healthy. Ekeler is a good between tackles runner that can get downhill in a hurry. He is a solid one-cut runner. He also catches the ball very well and can make plays in space.
87.outlook: Ekeler is not near the same back as past years but he has some value as a possible reserve back because of his work in the passing game. This gives him a decent weekly floor. He should get around 30 receptions and 600-plus total yards.

88.name: Brashard Smith
88.comment: Smith worked his way into a role his rookie season. He played every game and finished with 323 total yards. Smith got most of his chances in the passing game, catching 25 passes for 172 yards. Smith finished 61st overall in fantasy running back scoring. He had one game with double-digit fantasy points. Smith is likely in a similar reserve role this year, getting most of his chances as a third-down back. Smith is a very fast back with solid hands. He won't make a ton of plays on the inside, though, lacking some thump for the position.
88.outlook: Smith has minimal fantasy value. His numbers should be similar to last year, meaning he won't help most fantasy teams. He might get 20 receptions and 300 total yards.

89.name: LeQuint Allen
89.comment: Allen was mainly the No. 3 back for the Jaguars his rookie season. He didn't play much, getting 148 total yards. Allen is likely in a similar deep reserve role for this coming season. Allen has decent size but won't make a ton of plays after contact. He is a three-down back that might be better served as a pass catcher than receiver at this point of this career.
89.outlook: Allen has a little receiving potential but not much more. He could get 20 receptions and 300 or so total yards. That won't help a ton of fantasy owners.

90.name: AJ Dillon
90.comment: Dillon fell down the Eagles depth chart last year and barely saw the field as the No. 3 or 4 back. He played seven games, rushing 12 times for 60 yards. These were the lowest rushing totals of his career in a season he played. Dillon had 800-plus total yards three straight seasons before his last two seasons. His career hasn't quite progressed as expected but Dillon can still serve a backup role well. Dillon is a big, power back that does his best work between the tackles. He is a load to bring down because of his size. He doesn't have a lot of speed to make plays on the outside but is more than capable. He is an improved pass catcher, but does not excel in that role.
90.outlook: Dillon is trending the wrong way. He is not worth a roster spot. His numbers will be pretty ho-hum in a reserve role.

91.name: Joe Mixon
91.comment: Mixon was unable to play at all last season because of some mysterious foot/ankle injury. He is apparently going to attempt to play this year but nothing is certain about his status. Mixon is no sure thing to return. And if he is battling some sort of injury, you would think his days of starting might be about over. Mixon might be best served in a platoon role if he is able to make his return to the NFL. He had two straight 1,000-yard rushing seasons before last year and has five for his career. When healthy and on his game, Mixon is a big-play back that can get to the next level in a hurry and has the size to carry the load for three downs. He is a good pass catcher out of the backfield and improved inside runner from earlier in his career.
91.outlook: Mixon is a huge wild card. It isn't even certain he will play at all. And if he plays, what is his exact role? Take him as a reserve back and hope for the best.

92.name: Emari Demercado
92.comment: Demercado was third on the depth chart to open the season for the Cardinals but got moved up because of injury. He got some work in 13 games, finishing with 413 total yards and a touchdown. He had two games with double-digit fantasy points. But despite all the injuries at running back, Demercado still didn't earn a ton of work, which isn't great for his future. He signed with the Chiefs this offseason and will look to earn a reserve role with his new team. He has finished with similar numbers each of his three seasons in the NFL. Demercado has very good speed for the position. He isn't the biggest back, though, so durability is a bit of a concern. He also won't make a ton of plays between the tackles.
92.outlook: Demercado will get a few weekly touches, but have little fantasy value unless injury hits. He might have some late-round value as a reserve back. Demercado can get around 300 total yards and a few scores.

93.name: Chris Brooks
93.comment: Brooks was with the Packers for a second straight season and played every game. He had 197 total yards. He got most of his chances the last week of the season, rushing 13 times for 61 yards. Brooks has never had more than 260 total yards in three NFL seasons. Brooks will look to move up the depth chart and play a bigger role offensively, which is possible but doesn't seem too likely. Brooks looks the part at running back. He has good size and strength. He can hit the hole in a hurry and make plays after contact. He doesn't have a lot of wiggle and is just a so-so pass catcher.
93.outlook: Brooks might get a few more touches, but probably not enough to be a fantasy factor. He could be worth monitoring but likely isn't worth a draft spot just yet. He could get 300 total yards with a score or two.

94.name: Kyle Juszczyk
94.comment: Juszczyk continues to be one of the top fullbacks in the league. He had 210 total yards and two touchdowns last season. He failed to reach double-digit fantasy points in a single game but did have 24 receptions, his highest total since 2021. Juszczyk is a good pass catcher and has good speed for a fullback. He excels as a blocker, though. He isn't likely getting many chances to run the ball but should continue to get receptions. He has at least 30 receptions five seasons.
94.outlook: Juszczyk has a little value in PPR formats but that is about it. He will get some weekly catches and a few scores. Expect around 20 receptions and 200 total yards with a few scores.

95.name: Zonovan Knight
95.comment: Knight saw a resurgence last season after not playing at all the previous year. He started eight games for the Cardinals because of injury and had 429 total yards. He did struggle some running the all, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry. He did well in the passing game, though, catching 22 passes for 160 yards. Knight is going to have a hard time getting that much work this year but showed he can serve a backup role well. He re-signed with the Cardinals after the season to likely serve as the No. 3 or 4 for the team. Knight is a smaller back but runs with some power. He catches the ball pretty well and has decent moves in space.
95.outlook: Knight is a big stretch for fantasy teams. He might be worth a look of waivers if he happens to get some playing time once again.

96.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
96.comment: McLaughlin moved down the depth chart last year and was even inactive some weeks. He played eight games, totaling 214 yards.
