He had 500-plus total yards each of his first two seasons before last year. He will look to earn a bigger role this year but nothing is certain. He is likely to get spot work as a change-of-pace back in Denver. McLaughlin is a small back but runs with some power and has good moves in space. He catches the ball well out of the backfield. He does lack some size to be an every-down back but can do well in spot duty.
96.outlook: McLaughlin has been little help to fantasy teams in each of his first three seasons. He is likely to finish with similar numbers this year. He might be worth a bench spot as a deep reserve back. Look for around 300 total yards and 10 receptions with a few scores.

97.name: Michael Carter
97.comment: Carter found his way into the starting lineup for the Cardinals last year because of injury, getting five starts. He had 600 total yards, his highest total since 2022. Carter had three games with double-digit fantasy points. He didn't exactly excel as the starter, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry for the season. Carter can serve the backup role well, though, and will challenge for that job with the Titans. Carter has some value because of his experience and skill set. Carter is small but has top speed and good moves in space. He catches the ball well and can be a real asset in the passing game. Carter lacks a little vision, though, and his size is a concern for his durability.
97.outlook: Carter has some potential for the big game if he happens to start once again because of his work in the passing game. You just never know when that big game might come, though. Expect around 300 total yards and a score or two.

98.name: DJ Giddens
98.comment: Giddens got in nine games his rookie season, serving as the No. 3 or 4 back most of his rookie year. He ran 26 times for 96 yards. Giddens will look to move up the depth chart this year and play a bigger role, looking to get that top backup job to Jonathan Taylor. Giddens is an explosive player that sets up his blocks well and hits the hole in a hurry. He really cuts well and can make defenders look silly because of that. He is not a three-down back, though, struggling to do much in the passing game. Giddens will need to improve in that area to play a bigger role in year two.
98.outlook: Entering 2025, Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor had missed 16 games in three prior seasons, so the team drafted DJ Giddens in the fifth round as a potential high-end depth option should the franchise tailback miss time. None of that line of thinking went as planned; Taylor made the Pro Bowl in a season where he played all 17 games and posted 1,963 scrimmage yards, and Giddens (26) was out-touched by Ameer Abdullah (30) to settle in as the team's RB3. Giddens' draft profile indicated he had just started playing football in his senior year of high school and was just 21 entering the 2025 NFL Draft, so a developmental year wasn't overly surprising. Now, Abdullah and Tyler Goodson were both let go in free agency, clearing the second-year back to compete with seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan for the backup job behind Taylor. According to Pro Football Focus, the former Kansas State running back was effective at 2.69 yards after contact per carry as a rusher but also logged just 22 snaps as a receiver, so the team might not trust him in pass protection. With that said, Giddens caught 50 passes for 581 yards in his final two collegiate seasons, so the catch-and-run aspect of his game might have potential. As RotoBaller's PPR rankings (223rd overall) suggest, the "6-foot", 212-pound slasher isn't a priority in drafts. Still, in deeper leagues, he could be a safety net for Taylor's managers - or those looking for a potential deep sleeper that is an injury away from starting. Indianapolis would likely be in the market for a veteran running back should something catastrophic happen to their starter, though.

99.name: Audric Estime
99.comment: Estime played with the Saints last year and got some chances late in the year because of injury. He had double-digit carries each of his last two games and topped 15 fantasy points each of those games. Estime had 301 total yards and a touchdown in seven games, including a start. He has 300-plus total yards each of his first two seasons in the NFL. Estime will look to earn a little bigger role from day one this year but likely will be the No. 3 or 4 back once again. Estime is a powerful runner. He does well after contact and can be a load to bring down once he gets going. He also is a decent pass catcher, being able to serve as a three-down back. He does lack a little wiggle and his burst is a little lacking for the position.
99.outlook: Estime probably isn't worth a draft pick but might be worth grabbing off waivers if he starts getting som chances. Estime can get 300 total yards and a touchdown or two.

100.name: Trevor Etienne
100.comment: Etienne was way down the depth chart for the Panthers his rookie season. He played every single game but manage just 107 total yards on 23 touches. He will look to move up the depth chart this year but nothing is certain after a disappointing rookie year. Etienne is an elusive back with plus speed. He is a little inexperienced at the position, though, and doesn't always do a good job of hitting the hole.
100.outlook: Etienne is going to get a few chances but seems a stretch for fantasy teams unless injury hits. He might get a 300 total yards and a few scores.
